1
姚鏌張嵿伍文定蔡天祐詹榮劉天和楊守禮張岳郭宗臯趙時春
Yao Mo, Zhang Dian, Wu Wending, Cai Tianyou, Zhan Rong, Liu Tianhe, Yang Shouli, Zhang Yue, Guo Zonggao, and Zhao Shichun
2
姚鏌，字英之，慈溪人。 弘治六年進士。 除禮部主事，進員外郎。 擢廣西提學僉事。 立宣成書院，延《五經》師以教士子。 桂人祀山魈卓旺。 鏌毀像，俗遂變。 遷福建副使，未幾改督學政。 正德九年擢貴州按察使。 十五年拜右副都御史，巡撫延綏。 上邊務六事，皆議行。 嘉靖元年，吉囊入涇陽。 鏌遣遊擊彭楧出西路，釋指揮卜雲于獄，使副之。 夜半邀擊，斬其二將，乃遁。 璽書褒諭。 尋召為工部右侍郎，出督漕運，改兵部左侍郎。
Yao Mo, styled Yingzhi, was a native of Cixi. He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of the Hongzhi reign. He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites and later promoted to assistant department director. He was promoted to assistant education intendant of Guangxi. He founded Xuancheng Academy and invited teachers of the Five Classics to instruct students. The people of Gui worshipped a mountain spirit called Zhuo Wang. Mo destroyed its image, and local custom accordingly changed. He was transferred to vice commissioner of Fujian, and before long was reassigned to supervise educational affairs. In the ninth year of the Zhengde reign he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou. In the fifteenth year he was appointed vice censor-in-chief of the right and grand coordinator of Yan-Sui. He submitted six proposals on frontier affairs, all of which were debated and implemented. In the first year of the Jiajing reign, Jirong invaded Jingyang. Mo dispatched mobile corps commander Peng Zhuan along the western route, released commander Bu Yun from prison, and had him serve as his deputy. At midnight they ambushed the enemy, beheaded two of their generals, and the raiders then withdrew. An imperial edict under seal commended him. Soon afterward he was summoned to serve as vice minister of the right in the Ministry of Works, sent out to supervise grain transport, and then transferred to vice minister of the left in the Ministry of War.
3
四年，遷右都御史，提督兩廣軍務兼巡撫。 田州土官岑猛謀不軌。 鏌調永順、保靖兵，使沈希儀與張經、李璋、張佑、程鑒各統兵八萬，分道討。 而鏌與總兵官硃麒等攻破定羅、丹梁。 用希儀計，結猛婦翁岑璋使為內應，大破之，斬猛子邦彥。 璋誘殺猛，獻其首。 詔進鏌左都御史，加太子少保，任一子官，諸將進秩有差。 鏌請改設流官，陳善後七事，制可。 乃命參議汪必東、僉事申惠與參將張經以兵萬人鎮其地。 必東、惠移疾他駐。 猛党盧蘇、王受等詐言猛不死，借交阯兵二十萬且至，夷民信之。 蘇等薄城，經突圍走，城遂陷。 王受亦攻入思恩府。 巡按御史石金劾鏌失策罔上，並論前總督盛應期。 帝以鏌有功，許便宜撫剿。 蘇、受數求赦，鏌不許，將大討之。 會廷議起王守仁督兩廣軍，令鏌與同事。 鏌引疾乞罷，許馳驛歸。
In the fourth year he was transferred to censor-in-chief of the right, placed in charge of military affairs in the two Guang provinces, and concurrently appointed grand coordinator. Cen Meng, the native official of Tianzhou, plotted rebellion. Mo mobilized troops from Yongshun and Baojing and placed Shen Xiyi, Zhang Jing, Li Zhang, Zhang You, and Cheng Jian each in command of eighty thousand men to attack along separate routes. Meanwhile Mo, together with commander-in-chief Zhu Qi and others, captured Dingluo and Danliang. Following Shen Xiyi's plan, he won over Meng's father-in-law Cen Zhang as an inside collaborator, inflicted a major defeat, and beheaded Meng's son Bangyan. Zhang lured Meng to his death and presented Meng's head. An edict promoted Mo to left censor-in-chief, granted him the additional title junior guardian of the heir apparent, appointed one of his sons to office, and advanced the various generals in rank according to merit. Mo requested that the post be converted to regular officials and submitted seven measures for long-term pacification; the court approved. He then ordered participating secretary Wang Bidong, assistant surveillance commissioner Shen Hui, and assistant regional commander Zhang Jing to garrison the area with ten thousand troops. Wang Bidong and Shen Hui relocated elsewhere on pretext of illness. Meng's partisans Lu Su and Wang Shou falsely claimed that Meng was still alive and that two hundred thousand troops from Jiaozhi were on their way; the native populace believed them. Lu and his followers pressed the city; Zhang Jing broke through and fled, and the city fell. Wang Shou also attacked and seized Si'en Prefecture. Investigating censor Shi Jin memorialized that Mo's strategy had failed and deceived the throne, and also criticized the former grand coordinator Sheng Yingqi. The emperor, considering Mo's merits, allowed him discretionary authority to pacify or suppress as needed. Lu and Wang repeatedly sought pardon, but Mo refused and prepared a major punitive campaign. The court decided to recall Wang Shouren to oversee the Guang armies and ordered Mo to serve jointly with him. Mo cited illness and requested dismissal; he was permitted to return home by imperial courier relay.
4
初，廣東提學道魏校毀諸寺觀田數千畝，盡入霍韜、方獻夫諸家。 鏌至廣，追還之官。 韜、獻夫恨甚，與張璁、桂萼合排鏌。 謂大同當征而反撫，田州當撫而反征，皆費宏謀國不臧，釀成南北患。 時宏雖去，猶借鏌以排之也。 鏌既得請，方候代，千夫長韋貴、徐伍攻復思恩。 鏌上其狀。 詔先賞貴等，而以撫剿事宜俟守仁處置。 既而鏌奏辯石金前疏，詆金阻撓養寇。 金亦再疏詆鏌。 帝先入璁等言，落鏌職閑住。
Earlier, Wei Xiao of the Guangdong education circuit had confiscated several thousand mu of temple and monastery land, all of which ended up in the households of Huo Tao, Fang Xianfu, and others. When Mo arrived in Guangdong, he recovered the lands for the government. Huo and Fang hated him deeply and, together with Zhang Cong and Gui E, combined to attack Mo. They charged that Datong should have been suppressed but was instead pacified, and Tianzhou should have been pacified but was instead attacked—all owing to Fei Hong's unsound statecraft, which had bred troubles north and south. Though Hong had already left office, they still used Mo to strike at him. After Mo had obtained his dismissal and was awaiting his replacement, company commanders Wei Gui and Xu Wu attacked and recovered Si'en. Mo reported their action to the throne. An edict first rewarded Gui and the others, while pacification and suppression were left to Wang Shouren's disposition. Mo then memorialized in rebuttal to Shi's earlier memorial, accusing Shi of obstruction and of nurturing bandits. Shi again memorialized attacking Mo. The emperor, having already accepted Zhang Cong and the others' words, stripped Mo of office and ordered him to live in retirement.
5
其後，蘇、受復叛，帝漸思鏌。 十三年，三邊闕總制。 大學士費宏、李時同召對。 宏薦鏌，時亦助之。 遂命以兵部尚書總制三邊軍務。 未赴，宏卒。 鏌辭。 帝不悅，仍落職閑住。 鏌既罷，薦者至二十疏，不用。 家居數年卒。
Later, when Lu and Wang rebelled again, the emperor gradually came to miss Mo. In the thirteenth year the tri-border command was vacant. Grand secretaries Fei Hong and Li Shi were summoned together for audience. Hong recommended Mo, and Li Shi also supported him. Mo was therefore ordered to serve as minister of war with overall command of tri-border military affairs. Before he could take up the post, Hong died. Mo declined the appointment. The emperor was displeased and again stripped him of office for retirement. After Mo's dismissal, recommenders submitted as many as twenty memorials on his behalf, but he was not employed. He lived at home for several years and then died.
6
子淶，字維東。 嘉靖二年殿試第一。 授翰林修撰。 爭「大禮」，廷杖。 又議郊祀合祀，不當輕易。 召修《明倫大典》，懇辭不與。 累官侍讀學士。
His son Lai, styled Weidong, placed first in the palace examination of the second year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed Hanlin compiler. He disputed the Great Rites controversy and was beaten in court. He also argued that combining suburban sacrifices should not be done lightly. When summoned to compile the Minglun Dadian, he earnestly declined and did not participate. He rose cumulatively to attendant reader.
7
張嵿，字時俊，蕭山人。 成化二十三年進士。 弘治初，修《憲宗實錄》，命往蘇、松諸府采軼事。 事竣，授上饒知縣。 遷南京兵部主事，就進刑部郎中。 正德初，遷興化知府。 隆平侯張祐無子，弟祿與族人爭襲，訴于南京法司，久不決，復訴京師。 劉瑾方擅政，遂削尚書樊瑩、都御史高銓籍。 嵿以郎承勘，為民。 瑾敗，起知南雄。 擢江西參政，進右布政使。 舉治行卓異，遷左。 甯王宸濠欲拓地，廣其居，嵿執不可。 大恚，遣人饋之。 嵿發視，則棗梨姜芥，蓋隱語也。 未幾，召為光祿卿。 以右副都御史巡撫保定諸府，忤中貴，移疾歸。
Zhang Dian, styled Shijun, was a native of Xiaoshan. He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-third year of the Chenghua reign. Early in the Hongzhi reign, while compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong, he was ordered to the prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang to collect anecdotes. When the task was finished, he was appointed magistrate of Shangrao. He was transferred to principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of War and concurrently promoted to director in the Ministry of Justice. Early in the Zhengde reign he was transferred to prefect of Xinghua. Marquis Longping Zhang You had no son; his younger brother Lu contested the succession with clansmen, suing before the Nanjing judiciary without resolution for a long time, then suing again in the capital. Liu Jin was then monopolizing power and stripped minister Fan Ying and censor-in-chief Gao Quan of their registers. Dian, as the director carrying out the investigation, was reduced to commoner status. When Jin fell, he was reinstated as prefect of Nanxiong. He was promoted to administrative commissioner of Jiangxi and advanced to right provincial administration commissioner. Recognized for outstanding governance, he was transferred to the left post. Prince of Ning Chen Hao wished to expand his territory and enlarge his residence; Dian firmly refused. Greatly enraged, the prince sent someone to present gifts to him. When Dian opened them, they were jujubes, pears, ginger, and mustard—a hidden message meaning he should be beaten and bound. Before long he was summoned to serve as director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments. As vice censor-in-chief of the right he grand-coordinated the prefectures of Baoding and others; he offended the eunuch power-brokers and retired on grounds of illness.
8
伍文定，字時泰，松滋人。 父琇，貴州參議。 文定登弘治十二年進士。 有膂力，便弓馬，議論慷慨。 授常州推官，精敏善決獄，稱強吏。 魏國公徐俌與民爭田，文定勘，歸之民。 劉瑾入俌重賄，興大獄，巡撫艾朴以下十四人悉被逮。 文定已遷成都同知，亦下詔獄，斥為民。 瑾敗，起補嘉興。
Wu Wending, styled Shitai, was a native of Songzi. His father Xiu was an administrative commissioner of Guizhou. Wending passed the metropolitan examination in the twelfth year of the Hongzhi reign. He was physically strong, skilled with bow and horse, and spoke with generous conviction. Appointed reviewing official of Changzhou, he was acute and skilled at deciding cases, and was known as a formidable magistrate. The duke of Wei, Xu Fu, contested land with commoners; Wending investigated and returned it to the people. Liu Jin accepted heavy bribes from Fu and launched a major prosecution; grand coordinator Ai Pu and fourteen others below him were all arrested. Wending had already been transferred to subprefect of Chengdu; he too was thrown into the imperial prison and banished as a commoner. When Jin fell, he was reinstated at Jiaxing.
9
江西姚源賊王浩八等流劫浙江開化，都御史俞諫檄文定與參將李隆、都指揮江洪、僉事儲珊討之，軍華埠。 而都指揮白弘與湖州知府黃衷別營馬金。 賊党劉昌三破，執弘，官軍大挫。 浩八突華埠，洪、文定擊敗之，追及于孔埠。 隆、珊亦追至池淮，破其巢，進攻淫田。 洪以奇兵深入，中賊誘，與指揮張琳等皆被執。 文定等殿后得還，賊亦遁歸江西。 諫等上文定忠勇狀，詔所司獎勞。 擢河南知府，計擒劇賊張勇、李文簡。 以才任治劇，調吉安。 計平永豐及大茅山賊。 已，佐巡撫王守仁平桶岡、橫水。 宸濠反，吉安士民爭亡匿。 文定斬亡者一人，眾乃定。 乃迎守仁入城。 知府邢珣、徐璉、戴德孺等先後至，共討賊。 文定當大帥。 丙辰之戰，身犯矢石、火燎須不動。 賊平，功最，擢江西按察使。 張忠、許泰至南昌，欲冒其功，而守仁已俘宸濠赴浙江。 忠等失望，大恨。 文定出謁，遂縛之。 文定罵曰：「吾不恤九族，為國家平大賊，何罪？ 汝天子腹心，屈辱忠義，為逆賊報仇，法當斬。 」忠益怒，椎文定僕地。 文定求解任，不報。
Bandits of Yaoyuan in Jiangxi, Wang Haoba and others, raided Kaihua in Zhejiang; censor-in-chief Yu Jian ordered Wending, together with regional commander Li Long, regional commander-in-chief Jiang Hong, and surveillance commissioner Chu Shan, to suppress them; the army encamped at Huabu. Meanwhile regional commander-in-chief Bai Hong and the prefect of Huzhou, Huang Zhong, separately encamped at Majin. The bandit partisan Liu Chang defeated them three times, captured Hong, and the government army suffered a major setback. Haoba rushed Huabu; Hong and Wending defeated him and pursued as far as Kongbu. Long and Shan also pursued to Chihuai, destroyed their nest, and advanced to attack Yintian. Hong led elite troops deep into enemy territory and fell into an ambush; he and commander Zhang Lin and others were all captured. Wending and others brought up the rear and got back safely; the bandits also fled to Jiangxi. Yu and others submitted a memorial on Wending's loyalty and bravery; an edict ordered the relevant office to reward him. He was promoted to prefect of Henan and through stratagem captured the notorious bandits Zhang Yong and Li Wenjian. Because of his ability he was assigned to govern a difficult prefecture and was transferred to Ji'an. By stratagem he pacified the bandits of Yongfeng and Mount Damao. Thereafter, he assisted Grand Coordinator Wang Shouren in pacifying Tonggang and Hengshui. When Chen Hao rebelled, the gentry and common people of Ji'an scrambled to flee and hide. Wending executed one man who tried to flee, and the people then settled down. He then welcomed Shouren into the city. The prefects Xing Xun, Xu Lian, Dai Deru, and others arrived in succession and joined in the campaign against the rebels. Wending served as supreme commander. In the Battle of Bingchen, he personally braved arrows and stones; when fire singed his beard, he did not flinch. When the rebels were pacified, his merit ranked highest, and he was promoted to regional inspector of Jiangxi. Zhang Zhong and Xu Tai arrived at Nanchang, hoping to claim the credit for themselves, but Shouren had already captured Chen Hao and was escorting him to Zhejiang. Zhong and the others were disappointed and filled with bitter resentment. When Wending went out to pay his respects, they bound him on the spot. Wending reviled them, saying: "I care nothing for the destruction of my entire clan. I pacified a great rebel for the state—what crime have I committed? You are the Son of Heaven's closest confidants, yet you humiliate loyal men and avenge a rebel traitor. By law you deserve execution. " Zhong grew even angrier and struck Wending, knocking him to the ground. Wending requested to be relieved of his post, but received no reply.
10
尋遷廣東右布政使。 未赴，而世宗嗣位。 上忠等罪狀，且曰：「曩忠、泰與劉暉至江西，忠自稱天子弟，暉稱天子兒，泰稱威武副將軍，與天子同僚。 折辱命吏，誣害良民。 需求萬端，漁獵盈百萬。 致餓殍遍野，盜賊縱橫。 雖寸斬三人，不足謝江西百姓。 今大憝江彬、強尼皆已伏法，三人實其黨與。 乞速正天誅，用章國典。 」又請發宸濠資財，還之江西，以資經費； 矜釋忠、泰所陷無辜及甯府宗人不預謀者，以清冤獄。 帝並嘉納之。 論功，進右副都御史，提督操江。 嘉靖三年，討獲海賊董效等二百餘人，賜敕獎勞。 尋謝病歸。
Before long he was transferred to right provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong. Before he could take up the post, the Shizong Emperor succeeded to the throne. He submitted an account of the crimes of Zhong and the others, saying: "When Zhong, Tai, and Liu Hui came to Jiangxi, Zhong styled himself the Son of Heaven's younger brother, Hui styled himself the Son of Heaven's son, and Tai styled himself Deputy General of Military Majesty, putting himself on equal footing with the Son of Heaven. They humiliated appointed officials and falsely persecuted innocent people. Their demands were endless, and their extortion exceeded a million. The result was starving corpses strewn across the countryside and bandits running rampant. Even if the three were executed by dismemberment, it would not be enough to atone to the people of Jiangxi. Now the great villain Jiang Bin and the monk Qiang Ni have both been executed, and these three men were in fact their associates. I beg that they be swiftly punished according to law, so that the authority of the state may be upheld. " He also requested that Chen Hao's assets be disbursed and returned to Jiangxi to cover expenses; and that the innocent people framed by Zhong and Tai, together with Princely Ning clansmen who had not taken part in the plot, be shown mercy and released, so as to clear wrongful cases. The emperor approved and accepted all of these proposals. When merits were assessed, he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief of the right and appointed superintendent of river defense. In the third year of Jiajing, he captured more than two hundred sea bandits including Dong Xiao, and was granted an imperial edict commending his service. Before long he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
11
六年召拜兵部右侍郎。 其冬擢右都御史，代胡世寧掌院事。 雲南士酋安銓反，敗參政黃昭道，攻陷尋甸、嵩明。 明年，武定土酋鳳朝文亦反，殺同知以下官，與銓合兵圍雲南。 詔進文定兵部尚書兼前職，提督雲南、四川、貴州、湖廣軍討之，以侍郎梁材督餉。 會芒部叛酋沙保子普奴為亂，並以屬文定。 文定未至雲南，銓等已為巡撫歐陽重所破，遂移師征普奴。 左都御史李承勳極言川、貴殘破，不當用兵，遂召還，命提督京營。 文定至湖廣，疏乞省祭歸。 已，四川巡按御史戴金復上言：「叛酋稱亂之初，勢尚可撫。 而文定決意進兵，一無顧惜。 飛芻挽糧，糜數十萬。 及有詔罷師，尚不肯已。 又極論土酋阿濟等罪。 軍民訛言，幾復生變。 臣愚以為文定可罪也。 」尚書方獻夫、李承勳因詆文定好大喜功，傷財動眾，乃令致仕。
In the sixth year he was summoned and appointed vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War. That winter he was promoted to censor-in-chief of the right, replacing Hu Shining as head of the Censorate. The tribal chieftain An Quan of Yunnan rebelled, defeated assistant administrator Huang Zhaodao, and captured Xundian and Songming. The next year the tribal chieftain Feng Chaowen of Wuding also rebelled, killed officials down to the sub-prefect, and joined forces with Quan to besiege Yunnan. An edict promoted Wending to minister of war while retaining his previous post, and appointed him to supervise the armies of Yunnan, Sichuan, Guizhou, and Huguang in suppressing the rebels; Vice Minister Liang Cai was assigned to oversee supplies. At the same time Pu Nu, son of the rebel chieftain Sha Bao of Mangbu, was also in revolt, and he too was placed under Wending's command. Before Wending reached Yunnan, Quan and the others had already been defeated by Grand Coordinator Ouyang Chong, so he shifted his army to campaign against Pu Nu. Left Censor-in-Chief Li Chengxun strongly argued that Sichuan and Guizhou were devastated and that military force should not be used; Wending was thereupon recalled and ordered to supervise the capital garrison. When Wending reached Huguang, he memorialized requesting leave to return home for ancestral sacrifices. Shortly thereafter, Sichuan surveillance censor Dai Jin memorialized again: "When the rebel chieftain first rose in revolt, the situation could still have been settled through appeasement. Yet Wending resolved to advance troops and showed no regard for the consequences. Forage was rushed forward and grain transported at a gallop, squandering several hundred thousand in funds. Even after an edict ordered the army withdrawn, he still refused to stop. He also argued at length for the guilt of the tribal chieftain Aji and others. False rumors spread among soldiers and civilians, and unrest nearly broke out again. In my humble opinion, Wending deserves to be punished. " Ministers Fang Xianfu and Li Chengxun thereupon denounced Wending for seeking grand achievements at the cost of wasting resources and mobilizing large forces, and he was ordered to retire from office.
12
文定忠義自許，遇事敢為，不與時俯仰。 芒部之役，憤小丑數亂，欲為國伸威，為議者旁撓。 廟堂專務姑息，以故功不克就。 九年七月卒於家。 天啟初，追諡忠襄。
Wending prided himself on loyalty and righteousness, acted boldly when the occasion demanded, and would not trim his conduct to suit the times. In the Mangbu campaign, indignant that petty rebels repeatedly caused disorder, he wished to uphold the state's authority, but was thwarted by critics who interfered from the side. The court devoted itself solely to appeasement, and for this reason his achievements could not be brought to completion. In the seventh month of the ninth year he died at home. At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was posthumously given the temple name Zhongxiang.
13
邢珣，當塗人，弘治六年進士。 正德初，曆官南京戶部郎中。 忤劉瑾，除名。 瑾誅，起南京工部，遷贛州知府。 招降劇盜滿總等，授廬給田，撫之甚厚。 後討他盜，多藉其力。 守仁征橫水、桶岡，珣常為軍鋒。 功最，增二秩。 宸濠反，以重賞誘總。 總執其使送珣，遂從珣共平宸濠。
Xing Xun was a native of Dangtu and passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of the Hongzhi reign. At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he served as a bureau director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue. He offended Liu Jin and was dismissed from office. When Jin was executed, he was reappointed to the Nanjing Ministry of Works and later transferred to prefect of Ganzhou. He induced the notorious bandit Man Zong and others to surrender, granted them dwellings and fields, and treated them with great generosity. Later, in campaigns against other bandits, he often relied on their help. When Shouren campaigned against Hengshui and Tonggang, Xun often served as the army's vanguard. His merit ranked highest, and he was promoted two ranks. When Chen Hao rebelled, he tried to lure Man Zong with rich rewards. Zong seized Chen Hao's envoy and delivered him to Xun, then followed Xun in jointly suppressing Chen Hao's rebellion.
14
徐璉，朝邑人。 文定同年進士。 由戶部郎中出為袁州知府。 從討宸濠，獲首功千餘。 事定，珣、璉遷江西右參政。 世宗錄功，各增秩二等。 嘉靖二年大計，給事御史劾監司不職者二十二人，珣、璉與焉。 吏部以軍功未酬，請進秩布政使致仕，從之。 二人竟廢。
Xu Lian was a native of Chaoyi. He passed the metropolitan examination in the same year as Wending. After serving as a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, he was appointed prefect of Yuanzhou. He took part in the campaign against Chen Hao and claimed more than a thousand enemy heads for merit. When the affair was settled, Xun and Lian were transferred to right assistant administrator of Jiangxi. The Shizong Emperor recorded their merits, and each was promoted two ranks. At the grand assessment in the second year of Jiajing, supervising secretaries and censors impeached twenty-two surveillance and administration officials for dereliction of duty; Xun and Lian were among them. The Ministry of Personnel, noting that their military merit had not been properly rewarded, requested that they be promoted to provincial administration commissioner and allowed to retire; the request was approved. In the end, both men were cast aside.
15
珣子埴嘗學于張璁。 嘉靖初登鄉薦。 璁貴顯，屢欲援之，辭不應。 授浦城知縣。 有徐浦者，役公府。 埴一見異之，令與子同學，為娶妻。 後登第為給事中。 其家世世祀埴。 弟址，進士，曆御史，終山東鹽運使。 以清操聞。
Xun's son Zhi had once studied under Zhang Cong. At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he passed the provincial examination. When Cong rose to high prominence, he repeatedly tried to advance Zhi's career, but Zhi declined. He was appointed magistrate of Pucheng. There was a man named Xu Pu who served in the prefectural office. At first sight Zhi recognized his exceptional talent, had him study together with his son, and found him a wife. Later he passed the metropolitan examination and became a supervising secretary. His family worshipped Zhi in every generation. His younger brother Zhi was a jinshi, served successively as a censor, and ended his career as salt transport commissioner of Shandong. He was known for his integrity.
16
戴德孺，臨海人。 弘治十八年進士。 曆工部員外郎。 監蕪湖稅，有清名。 再遷臨江知府。 宸濠反，遣使收府印，德孺斬之。 與家人誓曰：「吾死守孤城。 脫有急，若輩沉池中，吾不負國也。 」即日戒嚴。 旋與守仁共滅宸濠。 以憂去。 世宗以德孺馭軍最整，獨增三秩，為雲南右布政使。 舟次徐州，覆水死。 後贈光祿寺卿，予一子官。
Dai Deru was a native of Linhai. He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of the Hongzhi reign. He served as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Works. He supervised the Wuhu tax levy and earned a reputation for integrity. He was later transferred to prefect of Linjiang. When Chen Hao rebelled, he sent an envoy to seize the prefectural seal; Deru executed the envoy. He swore an oath with his family, saying: "I shall die defending this isolated city. If danger comes, you must all drown yourselves in the pool. I will not fail the state. " That same day he imposed martial law. Shortly thereafter he joined Shouren in suppressing Chen Hao's rebellion. He left office on grounds of grief. The Shizong Emperor, noting that Deru had commanded troops with the greatest discipline, alone promoted him three ranks and appointed him right provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan. When his boat stopped at Xuzhou, it capsized and he drowned. Later he was posthumously granted the title director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and one son was granted an official post.
17
珣、璉等倡義討賊，月余成大功。 當事者以嫉守仁故，痛裁抑之。 或賞或否，又往往借考功法逐之去。 守仁之再疏辭爵也，為諸人訟曰：
Xun, Lian, and the others took the lead in rallying the righteous cause against the rebels, and in little more than a month achieved a great victory. Those in power, envying Shouren, severely curtailed and suppressed them. Some were rewarded and some were not; moreover they were often driven from office by exploiting the merit-assessment regulations. When Shouren twice memorialized declining enfeoffment, he pleaded on behalf of these men, saying:
18
宸濠變初起，勢焰猖熾，人心疑懼退阻。 當時首從義師，自伍文定、邢珣、徐璉、戴德孺諸人外，又有知府陳槐、曾璵、胡堯元等，知縣劉源清、馬津、傅南喬、李美、李楫及楊材、王冕、顧佖、劉守緒、王軾等，鄉官都御史王懋中，編修鄒守益，御史張鰲山、伍希儒、謝源等。 或摧鋒陷陣，或遮邀伏擊，或贊畫謀議，監錄經紀，所謂同功一體者也。 帳下之士，若聽選官雷濟，已故義官蕭禹，致仕縣丞龍光，指揮高睿，千戶王佐等，或詐為兵檄以撓其進止，壞其事機，或偽書反間以離其心腹，散其黨與。 今聞紀功文冊，改造者多所刪削。 舉人冀元亨為臣勸說甯王，反為奸人構陷，竟死獄中，尤傷心慘目，負之冥冥之中者。
When Chen Hao's rebellion first broke out, its momentum was wildly fierce, and people's hearts were filled with doubt and fear, inclined to retreat and hold back. At the time, those who were first to join the righteous army included, besides Wu Wending, Xing Xun, Xu Lian, Dai Deru, and others, the prefects Chen Huai, Zeng Yu, and Hu Yaoyuan; the magistrates Liu Yuanqing, Ma Jin, Fu Nanqiao, Li Mei, and Li Ji, along with Yang Cai, Wang Mian, Gu Yi, Liu Shouxu, and Wang Shi; the local official censor-in-chief Wang Maozhong; the compiler Zou Shouyi; and the censors Zhang Aoshan, Wu Xiru, and Xie Yuan. Some smashed through enemy lines; others laid ambushes; still others advised on strategy and managed records and logistics—they were, as the saying goes, partners in a single achievement. Among the men in his command—Clerk-of-Selection Lei Ji, the late honorary official Xiao Yu, retired assistant magistrate Long Guang, commander Gao Rui, centurion Wang Zuo, and others—some forged military orders to disrupt the enemy's movements and ruin their plans, while others sent forged letters to sow discord among their inner circle and break up their faction. I have now learned that in the records of merit, those who revised them have cut away much. The presented scholar Ji Yuanheng, who on my behalf had tried to persuade the Prince of Ning, was instead framed by wicked men and died in prison—a sight especially heartbreaking to behold; I owe him a debt in the world beyond.
19
夫宸濠積威淩劫，雖在數千里外，無不震駭失措。 而況江西諸郡縣切近剝床，觸目皆賊兵，隨處有賊黨，非真有捐軀赴難之義，戮力報主之忠，孰肯甘齏粉之禍，從赤族之誅，蹈必死之地，以希萬一難冀之功乎！
Chen Hao's long-standing prestige and intimidation were such that even thousands of li away, no one failed to be shaken with terror and thrown into confusion. How much more so in Jiangxi's prefectures and counties, pressed hard on every side—rebel soldiers wherever one looked, rebel sympathizers at every turn. Without genuine willingness to sacrifice one's life in crisis and to serve the throne with every ounce of one's strength, who would willingly face being ground to dust, bring down extermination on one's entire clan, and march into certain death—all for the slimmest chance of success?
20
今臣獨崇封爵，而此同事諸人者，或賞不行而並削其績，或賞未及而罰已先行，或虛受升職之名而因使退閑，或冒蒙不忠之號而隨以廢斥。 非獨為已斥諸權奸所誣構挫辱而已也。 群憎眾嫉，惟事指摘搜羅以為快，曾未見有鳴其不平、伸其屈抑者，臣竊痛之。
Now I alone have been raised in rank and ennobled, while these colleagues of mine—some received no reward and even had their accomplishments erased; some were punished before any reward could reach them; some received nominal promotions only to be pushed into retirement; some were falsely branded disloyal and then cast out. And this was not merely because they had already been slandered and framed by the ousted power brokers and brought to shame. Hatred and envy were everywhere; people took their pleasure in picking faults and digging up offenses, and I never saw anyone speak up for their grievances or defend what had been done to them—I grieve for this in my heart.
21
奏入，卒寢不行。
When the memorial was submitted, it was ultimately shelved and never acted upon.
22
蔡天祐，字成之，睢州人。 父晟，濟南知府，以廉惠聞。 天祐登弘治十八年進士，改庶起士，授吏科給事中，出為福建僉事。 曆山東副使，分巡遼陽。 歲歉，活饑民萬余。 辟濱海圩田數萬頃，民名之曰「蔡公田」。 累遷山西按察使。
Cai Tianyou, courtesy name Chengzhi, was a native of Suizhou. His father Sheng served as prefect of Jinan and was known for integrity and benevolence. Tianyou passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Hongzhi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel, and was later dispatched to serve as an assistant commissioner in Fujian. He served successively as vice commissioner of Shandong, with jurisdiction over Liaoyang. In a year of famine, he saved more than ten thousand starving people. He opened tens of thousands of qing of coastal polder fields, and the people called them "Lord Cai's Fields." He was repeatedly promoted until he became provincial surveillance commissioner of Shanxi.
23
嘉靖三年，大同兵亂，巡撫張文錦遇害。 詔曲赦亂卒，改巡撫宣府都御史李鐸撫之。 鐸以母憂不至，乃擢天祐右僉都御史，巡撫大同。 天祐從數騎馳入城，諭軍士獻首惡，眾心稍定。 會尚書金獻民、總兵官杭雄出師甘肅，道大同，亂卒疑見討，復鼓噪。 天祐懼，急請再赦。 兵部言「元惡不除無以警後」。 請特遣大臣總督宣、大軍務，以制其變。 乃命戶部侍郎胡瓚偕都督魯綱統京軍三千人以往。 瓚等未發而進士李枝齎餉銀至。 亂卒曰：「此承密詔盡殺大同人，為軍犒也。 」夜中火起，圍枝館，出牒示之乃解。 尋復殺知縣王文昌，圍代王府，脅王奏乞赦。 王急攜二郡王走宣府。 巡按御史王官言：「亂卒方囂，大兵壓境，是趣之叛也。 請亟止禁軍，容臣密圖。 」乃命瓚駐兵宣府。 頃之，天祐奏總兵官桂勇已捕五十四人，請止京軍勿遣。 帝責以阻撓，令必獲首惡郭鑒等。 既而瓚次陽和，勇、天祐令千戶苗登擒斬鑒等十一人，函首送瓚，請班師。
In the third year of Jiajing, the troops at Datong mutinied, and Grand Coordinator Zhang Wenjin was killed. An edict offered a partial amnesty to the mutinous troops and ordered Li Duo, censor-in-chief of Xuanfu, reassigned as grand coordinator, to pacify them. Li Duo did not arrive because he was in mourning for his mother, so Tianyou was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Datong. Tianyou rode into the city with only a few horsemen, urged the soldiers to hand over the ringleaders, and the people's hearts gradually settled. At that time Minister Jin Xianmin and Regional Commander Hang Xiong were leading troops to Gansu and passed through Datong; the mutinous soldiers suspected they had come to punish them and raised a clamor again. Tianyou was afraid and urgently requested another amnesty. The Ministry of War stated, "Unless the chief offenders are removed, there is no way to warn those who come after." They requested that a high minister be specially dispatched to take overall command of military affairs in Xuanfu and Datong so as to control the situation. Hu Zan, vice minister of Revenue, was therefore ordered to go with Regional Commander Lu Gang at the head of three thousand capital troops. Before Hu Zan and the others set out, presented scholar Li Zhi arrived bearing silver for military provisions. The mutinous soldiers said, "This silver, they say, comes under a secret edict to slaughter all the people of Datong as reward for the army." That night a fire broke out; they surrounded Li Zhi's lodging, and only when official documents were produced and shown to them did they disperse. Soon after they killed Magistrate Wang Wenchang, besieged the Princely Estate of Dai, and forced the prince to memorialize begging for amnesty. The prince hastily took two commandery princes and fled to Xuanfu. Touring Censor Wang Guan stated, "The mutinous troops are still rampant; with a large army pressing the border, this will only drive them to rebel." I beg that the capital troops be halted at once and that your subject be allowed to work out a secret plan." Hu Zan was therefore ordered to halt his troops at Xuanfu. Before long Tianyou memorialized that Regional Commander Gui Yong had already captured fifty-four men and requested that the capital troops not be dispatched. The Emperor rebuked him for obstruction and ordered that the ringleaders, Guo Jian and the others, must be captured without fail. Shortly thereafter Hu Zan halted at Yanghe; Gui Yong and Tianyou had Centurion Miao Deng capture and behead Jian and eleven others, sent the heads in a box to Hu Zan, and requested withdrawal of the army.
24
甫二日，鑒父郭疤子復糾徐氈兒等夜殺勇家人，又毀苗登家。 瓚言非盡殲不可。 帝乃切讓天祐，召勇還京，以故總兵硃振代之，敕瓚仍駐宣府。 居無何，天祐捕戮徐氈兒等，瓚等遂班師。 明年正月，侍郎李昆、孟春，總兵官馬永交章言疤子潛逃塞外，必為後患。 帝將遣使勘，會瓚還京言逃卒無足患，帝乃罷勘官勿遣。 疤子復潛入城，焚振第。 明旦，天祐閉城大索。 獲疤子及其黨三十四人，悉斬以徇。 盡宥脅從，人心乃大定。 事聞，賚銀幣。 已，進副都御史，巡撫如故。
Barely two days later, Jian's father Guo Bazi rallied Xu Zhan'er and others to kill Gui Yong's family by night and also destroyed Miao Deng's home. Hu Zan stated that unless the rebels were completely exterminated, the problem could not be solved. The Emperor then sharply rebuked Tianyou, recalled Gui Yong to the capital, replaced him with the former regional commander Zhu Zhen, and ordered Hu Zan to remain stationed at Xuanfu. Before long Tianyou captured and executed Xu Zhan'er and the others, whereupon Hu Zan and the others withdrew the army. In the first month of the following year, Vice Ministers Li Kun and Meng Chun and Regional Commander Ma Yong submitted memorials one after another stating that Bazi had slipped away beyond the frontier and would surely become a future menace. The Emperor was about to dispatch an envoy to investigate, but when Hu Zan returned to the capital and said the escaped soldiers were not worth worrying about, the Emperor cancelled the investigation and did not send the envoy. Bazi again slipped secretly into the city and burned Zhu Zhen's residence. At dawn the next day Tianyou closed the city and conducted a major search. They captured Bazi and thirty-four of his followers, and all were beheaded as a public warning. All who had been coerced were fully pardoned, and the people's hearts were greatly settled. When the matter was reported, he was granted silver and silks. Afterward he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief while continuing as grand coordinator.
25
尋就進兵部右侍郎。 久之，召還部。 天祐以籓祿久缺，又歲當繕邊垣，用便宜增淮鹽引價，每引萬加銀五千，被訐。 帝宥之。 至是，御史李宗樞復追論前事，天祐因引疾去。 居二年，奉詔起用。 未至京，得疾告歸，卒。 年九十五。
Before long he was promoted directly to vice minister of War. After a long time he was recalled to the ministry. Tianyou, because princely stipends had long gone unpaid and because it was the year when the border ramparts were to be repaired, used discretionary authority to raise the price of Huai salt certificates by five thousand taels of silver per certificate, and was impeached. The Emperor pardoned him. At this time Censor Li Zongshu again pursued prosecution of the earlier matter, and Tianyou therefore cited illness and resigned. Two years later he was summoned by imperial edict to serve again. Before reaching the capital he fell ill, requested to return home, and died. He was ninety-five years old.
26
天祐有才智。 兵變時。 左右皆賊耳目，幕府動靜悉知之。 天祐廣招星卜藝士往來軍中，因具得其情，卒賴以成功。 在鎮七年，威德大著，父老為立安輯祠。
Tianyou was talented and resourceful. During the military mutiny, those around him were all the rebels' eyes and ears; every movement at headquarters was known to them in full. Tianyou widely recruited astrologers, diviners, and artisans to come and go in the army, and thereby learned their situation in full; in the end he succeeded by relying on this. During seven years in the garrison his authority and virtue greatly stood forth, and the local elders built for him the Anji Shrine.
27
胡瓚，字伯珩，永平人。 進士。 官終南京工部尚書。
Hu Zan, courtesy name Boheng, was a native of Yongping. He was a jinshi. He rose at last to minister of Works at Nanjing.
28
張文錦，安丘人。 弘治十二年進士，授戶部主事。 正德初，為劉瑾所陷，逮系詔獄，斥為民。 瑾誅，起故官。 再遷郎中。 督稅陝西，條上籌邊裕民十事。 遷安慶知府。 度甯王宸濠必反，與都指揮楊銳為禦備計。 宸濠果反，浮江下。 文錦等慮其攻南都，令軍士登城詬之。 宸濠乃留攻，卒不能克。 事具《楊銳傳》。 璽書褒美，擢太僕少卿。 嘉靖元年，拜右副都御史，巡撫大同。 文錦性剛。 以拒賊得重名，遂銳意振刷，操切頗無序。 大同北四望平衍，寇至無可禦。 文錦曰：「寇犯宣府不能近鎮城者，以葛谷、白陽諸堡為外蔽也。 今城外即戰場，何以示重？ 」議於城北九十里外，增設五堡，曰水口、宣寧、只河、柳溝、樺溝。 參將賈鑒督役嚴，卒已怨。 及堡成，欲徙鎮卒二千五百家戍之。 眾憚行，請募新丁，僚吏鹹以為言。 文錦怒曰：「如此，則令不行矣。 鎮親兵先往，孰敢後！ 」親兵素遊惰有室。 聞當發，大恐。 請孑身往，得分番。 又不聽，嚴趣之。 鑒承風，杖其隊長。 諸邊卒自甘州五衛殺巡撫許銘，朝廷處之輕，頗無忌。 至是，卒郭鑒、柳忠等乘眾憤，遂倡亂。 殺賈鑒，裂其屍，走出塞，屯焦山墩。 文錦恐與外寇連，令副將時陳等招之入城，即索治首亂者。 郭鑒等大懼，復聚為亂，焚大同府門，入行都司縱獄囚，又焚都御史府門。 文錦逾垣走，匿博野王府第。 亂卒欲燔王宮。 王懼，出文錦。 郭鑒等殺之，亦裂其屍，遂焚鎮守總兵公署。 出故總兵硃振于獄，脅為帥。 時嘉靖三年八月也。 事聞，帝命侍郎李昆赦亂卒。 昆為文錦請恤典，不報，久之，文錦父政訟其子守安慶功，禮部為之請，終不許。 文錦妻李氏復上疏哀請。 帝怒，命執齎疏者治之。 副都御史陳洪謨言：「文錦僨事，朝廷戮之可也。 假手士卒，傳之四方，損國威不小。 」復降旨詰責。 自是，廷臣不敢言。 萬曆中，始贈右都御史。 天啟初，追諡忠湣。
Zhang Wenjin was a native of Anqiu. In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a secretary in the Bureau of Revenue. At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he was framed by Liu Jin, arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison, and dismissed as a commoner. After Jin was executed he was restored to his former post. He was promoted again to bureau director. While supervising tax collection in Shaanxi, he submitted in detail ten measures for securing the border and enriching the people. He was transferred to prefect of Anqing. He judged that the Prince of Ning Chen Hao would surely rebel and, together with Regional Commander Yang Rui, made preparations for defense. Chen Hao did rebel and sailed down the river. Wenjin and the others, fearing he would attack the Southern Capital, had soldiers mount the walls and revile him. Chen Hao therefore remained to besiege the city and in the end could not take it. The full account is in 《Biography of Yang Rui》. An imperial letter praised and commended him, and he was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud. In the first year of Jiajing he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Datong. Wenjin's temperament was hard. Because he had won a great reputation for resisting the rebels, he then set himself sharply to reform and discipline, yet his management was rather disorderly. North of Datong the land was flat and open in every direction; when invaders arrived there was nothing with which to resist them. Wenjin said, "When bandits invaded Xuanfu they could not approach the garrison city because fortresses such as Ge Valley and Baiyang served as outer screens." "Now the battlefield lies right outside the city—how is one to display weight and authority?" It was decided to add five fortresses ninety li north of the city, named Shuikou, Xuanning, Zhihe, Liugou, and Huagou. Assistant Regional Commander Jia Jian supervised the labor strictly, and the troops were already resentful. When the fortresses were completed, he wished to transfer twenty-five hundred garrison households to guard them. The men feared being sent there and requested that new recruits be hired instead; the subordinate officials all spoke on their behalf. Wenjin angrily said, "If it is like this, then orders will not be carried out." "The garrison's personal troops will go first—who would dare hang back!" The personal troops had always been idle and had families. When they heard they were to be dispatched, they were greatly alarmed. They requested to go alone without their families, serving in rotation. Again he would not listen and sharply pressed them to depart. Jia Jian took his cue and beat their squad leader. Frontier troops from the five guards of Ganzhou, who had killed Grand Coordinator Xu Ming, had been treated lightly by the court and were largely without fear. At this juncture soldiers Guo Jian, Liu Zhong, and others, riding the crowd's anger, incited the mutiny. They killed Jia Jian, tore his corpse apart, fled beyond the pass, and encamped at Jiaoshan Beacon. Wenjin feared they would join with foreign bandits; he ordered Vice General Shi Chen and others to lure them back into the city and then immediately demanded punishment of the ringleaders of the mutiny. Guo Jian and the others were terrified. They rallied again in mutiny, burned the gate of Datong Prefecture, entered the Regional Military Commission to release prisoners, and burned the gate of the censor-in-chief's yamen as well. Wenjin climbed over the wall and fled, hiding in the residence of the Prince of Boye. The mutinous soldiers threatened to burn the princely palace. The prince, in fear, handed Wenjin over. Guo Jian and his followers killed him, dismembered his corpse, and then burned the headquarters of the garrison commander-in-chief. They released the former commander-in-chief Zhu Zhen from prison and forced him to serve as their leader. This occurred in the eighth month of the third year of the Jiajing reign. When word reached the court, the emperor ordered Vice Minister Li Kun to pardon the mutinous soldiers. Kun requested posthumous honors for Wenjin, but received no reply. Long afterward, Wenjin's father Zheng petitioned regarding his son's merit in defending Anqing; the Ministry of Rites pleaded on his behalf, but the request was ultimately denied. Wenjin's wife, Lady Li, submitted another memorial pleading in grief. The emperor was enraged and ordered the bearer of the memorial seized and punished. Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Hongmo said, "Wenjin failed in his duty; the court could have executed him. But to leave the deed to common soldiers and let the story spread everywhere would have done no small harm to the prestige of the state." An edict was again issued rebuking him. From that time on, court officials did not dare speak out. During the Wanli reign, he was at last posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief. At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously given the temple name Zhongmin.
29
詹榮，字仁甫，山海衛人。 嘉靖五年進士。 授戶部主事，曆郎中。
Zhan Rong, styled Renfu, was a native of Shanhai Guard. He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Jiajing reign. He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to serve as a bureau director.
30
督餉大同，值兵變，殺總兵官李瑾。 總督劉源清率師圍城，久不下。 榮素有智略，善應變。 叛卒掠城中，無犯榮者。 週邊益急，榮密約都指揮紀振、遊擊戴濂、鎮撫王寧同盟討賊。 察叛卒馬升、楊麟無逆志，乃陽令寧持官民狀詣源清所，為叛卒乞原，而陰以榮謀告，請宥升、麟死，畀三千金，俾募死士自效。 會源清已罷，巡撫樊繼祖許之。 升、麟遂結心腹，擒首惡黃鎮等九人戮之。 榮乃開城門，延繼祖入，復捕斬二十六人。 錄功，擢光祿寺少卿，再遷太常寺少卿。
While supervising grain transport at Datong, he encountered a military mutiny in which Commander-in-Chief Li Jin was killed. Grand Coordinator Liu Yuanqing led troops to besiege the city, but for a long time could not bring it to surrender. Rong had long been known for his resourcefulness and was skilled at adapting to sudden change. The rebel soldiers plundered the city, yet none laid a hand on Rong. As the crisis deepened, Rong secretly arranged with Regional Commander Ji Zhen, Mobile Corps Commander Dai Lian, and Garrison Pacification Commissioner Wang Ning to join forces against the rebels. Seeing that the rebel soldiers Ma Sheng and Yang Lin had no real rebellious intent, he outwardly ordered Ning to carry petitions from officials and commoners to Yuanqing's camp to beg pardon for the rebels, while secretly revealing Rong's plan: spare Sheng and Lin, give them three thousand taels of gold, and let them recruit loyal fighters to prove themselves. By then Yuanqing had already been dismissed, and Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu agreed. Sheng and Lin then rallied trusted followers, seized the ringleaders Huang Zhen and eight others, and executed them. Rong then opened the city gates, welcomed Jizu inside, and captured and executed twenty-six more men. His merit was recorded, and he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then transferred again to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
31
二十二年，以右僉都御史巡撫甘肅。 魯迷貢使留甘州者九十余人，總兵官楊信驅以禦寇，死者十之一。 榮言：「彼以好來，而用之鋒鏑，失遠人心，且示中國弱。 」詔奪信官，槥死者送之歸。 番人感悅。 逾年，以大同巡撫趙錦與總兵官周尚文不相能，詔榮與錦易任。 俺答數萬騎入掠，榮與尚文破之黑山陽，進右副都御史。 寇復大舉犯中路，參將張鳳等陣歿。 榮與尚文及總督翁萬達嚴兵備陽和，而遣騎邀擊，多所殺傷，寇乃引去。 代府奉國將軍充灼行剽，榮奏奪其祿。 充灼等結小王子入寇，謀據大同。 榮告尚文捕得，皆伏辜。 榮以大同無險，乃築東路邊牆百三十八里，堡七，墩台百五十四。 又以守邊當積粟。 而近邊弘賜諸堡三十一所，延亙五百餘里，辟治之皆膏腴田，可數十萬頃。 乃奏請召軍佃作，復其租徭，移大同一歲市馬費市牛賦之； 秋冬則聚而遏寇。 帝立從焉。 寇入犯，與尚文破之彌陀山，斬一部長。
In the twenty-second year, he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Gansu with the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. More than ninety Rumi tribute envoys still at Ganzhou were driven by Commander-in-Chief Yang Xin to fight bandits, and one in ten of them died. Rong said, "They came in friendship, yet were sent into battle; this alienates distant peoples and shows the Middle Kingdom to be weak." An edict stripped Xin of his office, placed the dead in coffins, and sent them home. The frontier peoples were deeply moved. The following year, because Grand Coordinator Zhao Jin of Datong and Commander-in-Chief Zhou Shangwen could not work together, an edict ordered Rong and Jin to exchange posts. Altan Khan entered with tens of thousands of horsemen to raid; Rong and Shangwen defeated him south of Heishan, and Rong was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. The bandits again mounted a major assault on the central route, and Brigade Commander Zhang Feng and others fell in battle. Rong, Shangwen, and Grand Coordinator Weng Wanda rigorously prepared defenses at Yanghe while dispatching cavalry to intercept the enemy, killing and wounding many; the bandits then withdrew. Chongzhuo, a Fengguo General of the Prince of Dai's household, went about plundering; Rong memorialized to strip him of his stipend. Chongzhuo and others joined with the Little Prince to invade and plotted to seize Datong. Rong informed Shangwen, who captured them; all were duly punished. Because Rong considered Datong to lack natural defenses, he built one hundred thirty-eight li of border wall on the eastern route, along with seven forts and one hundred fifty-four beacon towers. He also held that defending the frontier required stockpiling grain. Moreover, the thirty-one forts such as Hongci along the near frontier stretched continuously for more than five hundred li; once cleared and developed, they were all fertile land amounting to several hundred thousand qing. He therefore memorialized requesting that troops be summoned to farm the land as tenants, with their rents and corvée exemptions restored, and that Datong's annual horse-purchase funds be redirected to buy oxen and distribute them; in autumn and winter they would gather to repel invaders. The emperor immediately approved the plan. When bandits invaded, he and Shangwen defeated them at Mount Mile and beheaded one tribal chief.
32
榮先以靖亂功，進兵部右侍郎，又以繕邊破敵，累被獎賚。 召還理部事，進左。 尚書趙廷瑞罷，榮署部務，奏行秋防十事。 已而翁萬達入為尚書，遭母喪，榮復當署部務，辭疾乞休。 帝怒，奪職閑住。 越二年卒。
Rong had first been promoted to Vice Minister of War for quelling the mutiny, and was repeatedly rewarded for fortifying the frontier and defeating the enemy. He was recalled to manage the ministry's affairs and promoted to Left Vice Minister. When Minister Zhao Tingrui was dismissed, Rong acted in the minister's stead and memorialized ten autumn defense measures for implementation. Soon afterward Weng Wanda entered the capital as minister; when he entered mourning for his mother, Rong was again expected to act in the minister's stead, but he pleaded illness and requested retirement. The emperor was enraged, stripped him of office, and ordered him to live in retirement. Two years later he died.
33
當榮之撫大同也，萬達為總督，尚文為總兵。 三人皆有才略，寇數入不能得志。 自後代者不能任，寇無歲不入躪邊，人益思榮等。 明年，俺答薄京師，萬達、榮皆已去。 論者謂二人在，寇未必至此。 萬曆中，榮孫延為順天通判，上書訟榮功。 贈工部尚書，予恤如制。
When Rong served as grand coordinator of Datong, Weng Wanda was supreme commander and Zhou Shangwen was commander-in-chief. All three were men of talent and strategy; though bandits raided repeatedly, they could not achieve their aims. Afterward their successors could not fill their shoes; bandits invaded the frontier every year, and people increasingly longed for Rong and his colleagues. The next year Altan Khan approached the capital; Weng Wanda and Zhan Rong had both already left office. Commentators said that had the two men still been in office, the bandits might never have come so close. During the Wanli reign, Rong's grandson Yan, serving as assistant prefect of Shuntian, submitted a memorial pleading Rong's merits. Rong was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works, and mourning stipends were granted according to regulation.
34
劉源清，字汝澄，東平人。 正德九年進士。 授進賢知縣。
Liu Yuanqing, styled Rucheng, was a native of Dongping. He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of the Zhengde reign. He was appointed magistrate of Jinxian.
35
宸濠反，源清積薪環室，命家人曰：「事急，火吾家。 」一僕逸，手刃以徇。 縣中諸惡少與賊通者，悉杖殺之。 宸濠妃弟婁伯歸上饒募兵，源清邀戮之。 賊檄至，立斬其使。 會余幹知縣馬津、龍津驛丞孫天祐亦起兵拒賊。 賊七殿下者，奪運舟于龍津，天祐與戰，殺數人。 賊党募兵過龍津，天祐追殺之，焚其舟。 婁氏家眾西下，亦為天祐所遏，擒七十餘人。 賊兵不敢經湖東以窺兩浙者，三人力也。 賊平，源清征為御史。 嘉靖改元，津亦入為御史。 津，滁州人。 終福建副使。 源清尋遷大理丞，謝病歸。
When Prince Ning Chen Hao rebelled, Yuanqing piled firewood around his rooms and told his household, "If matters grow urgent, burn our house." One servant escaped; he killed him with his own hand as a warning to the rest. He beat to death every delinquent youth in the county who had communicated with the rebels. Lou Bo, younger brother of Chen Hao's consort, returned to Shangrao to raise troops; Yuanqing intercepted and killed him. When a rebel proclamation arrived, he immediately beheaded its bearer. At the same time Magistrate Ma Jin of Yugan and Sun Tianyou, assistant at Longjin Post, also raised troops to resist the rebels. A rebel known as the Seventh Prince's son seized transport boats at Longjin; Tianyou fought him and killed several men. Rebel partisans raising troops passed through Longjin; Tianyou pursued them, killed them, and burned their boats. The Lou clan's household followers moving west were also blocked by Tianyou, who captured more than seventy men. That rebel troops did not dare pass east of the lake to threaten the two Zhe provinces was due to the efforts of these three men. When the rebellion was suppressed, Yuanqing was summoned to serve as a censor. When the Jiajing reign began, Ma Jin also entered the capital as a censor. Ma Jin was a native of Chuzhou. He ended his career as vice commissioner of Fujian. Yuanqing soon transferred to serve as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then returned home citing illness.
36
六年夏，以右僉都御史巡撫宣府。 滴水崖賊郭春據城叛，稱王。 源清遣卒捕之，為所覺。 副總兵劉淵令曰「止擒元惡」，以旗繞城而呼。 其黨皆散，春等自剄死。 總兵官郤永虐下，源清劾罷之。 進副都御史。 十二年，以邊警遷兵部左侍郎，總制宣、大、山西、保定諸鎮軍務。 大同總兵官李瑾浚天城左孤店濠四十里，趣工急。 卒王福勝等焚殺瑾，因焚巡撫潘亻放署。 亻放奏瑾激變，帝命源清同總兵郤永討之。 源清榜令解散。 而榜言五堡變，處之過寬，五堡遺孽大懼。 師次陽和，亻放等密捕亂卒杖死十餘人，系賊首王保等七十餘人以獻，請旋師。 源清懲昔胡瓚事，不欲已，以囚屬御史蘇祐。 囚妄言前總兵硃振失職首亂，且多引無辜。 源清遣參將趙綱入城大索。 城中訛言城且屠，亂卒遂鼓噪，殺千戶張欽。 會僉事孫允中自源清所至，諭源清意，撫慰之始定。 振前為亂卒所擁，實不反，詣源清自明。 不能白，發憤自殺。
In the summer of the sixth year, he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu with the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief. The bandit Guo Chun of Dishui Cliff seized the city in rebellion and declared himself king. Yuanqing dispatched soldiers to capture him, but they were discovered. Vice Commander Liu Yuan issued the order "Only capture the chief culprit" and, with banners unfurled, circled the city shouting the proclamation. His followers all dispersed; Chun and the others cut their own throats and died. Commander-in-Chief Xi Yong abused his subordinates; Yuanqing impeached him and had him dismissed. He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief. In the twelfth year, on account of frontier alarms he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of War and given overall command of military affairs in the garrisons of Xuanfu, Datong, Shanxi, and Baoding. Commander-in-Chief Li Jin of Datong excavated a forty-li moat at the left solitary post of Tiancheng, pressing the labor urgently. The soldiers Wang Fusheng and others burned and killed Jin, and also burned the yamen of Grand Coordinator Pan Fang. Pan Fang memorialized that Jin had provoked the mutiny; the emperor ordered Yuanqing together with Commander-in-Chief Xi Yong to suppress them. Yuanqing posted a proclamation ordering the mutineers to disperse. But the proclamation spoke of the Five Forts mutiny and said it had been treated too leniently; the surviving remnants of the Five Forts were terrified. When the army halted at Yanghe, Pan Fang and others secretly captured mutinous soldiers and beat more than ten to death, bound the rebel leaders Wang Bao and more than seventy others and presented them, and requested that the army withdraw. Yuanqing, chastened by the earlier affair of Hu Zan, did not wish to stop; he entrusted the prisoners to Censor Su You. The prisoners falsely claimed that the former commander-in-chief Zhu Zhen had failed in duty and started the mutiny, and implicated many innocent men besides. Yuanqing dispatched Brigade Commander Zhao Gang to enter the city and conduct a thorough search. A false rumor spread through the city that a massacre was imminent; the mutinous soldiers then erupted in uproar and killed Thousand-Household Commander Zhang Qin. As it happened Vice Commissioner Sun Yunzhong came from Yuanqing's camp, explained Yuanqing's intent, and only after pacifying them did the city settle down. Zhen had earlier been coerced by the mutinous soldiers and had not in fact rebelled; he went to Yuanqing to clear himself. Unable to clear his name, he killed himself in a fit of rage.
37
永兵至城下大掠，五堡遺孽遂盡反。 迎戰，殺遊擊曹安。 官軍攻據四關，晝夜圍擊。 亂卒出前參將黃鎮等於獄，奉為帥，死守。 亻放與鎮國將軍俊郐隱等登城，止毋攻。 俊郐隱出見永請緩兵，皆不聽。 允中縋城出，言將士妄殺狀。 源清叱曰：「汝為賊遊說耶！ 」欲囚之。 允中不敢歸。 源清因多設邏卒，遏王府及有司軍民章疏，而請益師至五萬。 帝命侍郎錢如京、都督江桓統京軍八千以往。 已忽悟，罷弗遣，專責源清、永討賊。 亻放馳疏言，將士妄殺激變，速旋師，亂中已。 源清亦詆亻放媚賊。 張孚敬主源清，侍郎顧鼎臣、黃綰言用兵謬，帝不能決。 城圍久大困，毀王府及諸廨舍供爨。 兵部復下安撫令，源清亦樹幟招降，叛卒稍稍自投。 首惡黃鎮等亦分日出見，乞通樵采路，永許諾。 翌日采薪者出，永悉執之。 城中人益懼，亂卒復叛，勾外寇為助。 永遇之，大敗而遁。 叛卒遂引寇十餘騎入城，指代府曰：「以此為那顏居。 」「那顏」者，華言大人也。 城中人聞之，皆巷哭。 明日，外寇攻東南二關，叛卒與犄角，官軍殊死戰，互有殺傷。 寇知叛卒不足賴，倒戈擊之，大詬而去。 是時，寇游騎南掠至朔、應。 源清請募九邊兵，增總制官禦之，己得一意攻城，帝不許。 源清乃百道攻，穴城，為毒煙熏死者相籍。 復請壅水灌之。 帝大不懌，奪其職閑住，以兵部侍郎張瓚代之。 瓚未至，郎中詹榮等已悉捕首惡。
When Yong's troops reached the city and looted it heavily, the surviving mutineers from the Five Forts rose in full revolt. They gave battle and killed Mobile Corps Commander Cao An. Government troops seized the four passes and pressed the siege day and night. The mutineers freed the former brigade commander Huang Zhen and others from prison, proclaimed them leaders, and resolved to hold the city at all costs. Pan Fang, State Stabilizing General Jun Guiyin, and others climbed the wall and called for a halt to the assault. Jun Guiyin went out to meet Yong and pleaded for a reprieve from military pressure, but his appeals went unheeded. Yunzhong was lowered by rope from the wall to report how the soldiers had been killing without cause. Yuanqing rebuked him: "Are you acting as an advocate for the rebels?" He meant to have him imprisoned. Yunzhong did not dare go back into the city. Yuanqing posted additional patrol guards, cut off memorials from the princely establishment and from officials, soldiers, and civilians alike, and asked that reinforcements be raised to fifty thousand men. The emperor ordered Vice Minister Qian Rujing and Regional Commander Jiang Huan to lead eight thousand capital troops to the scene. He soon thought better of it, canceled the dispatch, and held Yuanqing and Yong solely responsible for suppressing the rebels. Pan Fang sent an urgent memorial arguing that the soldiers' reckless killings had provoked the revolt, urging an immediate withdrawal of the army, and declaring that the turmoil among the mutineers had already subsided. Yuanqing in turn accused Pan Fang of appeasing the rebels. Zhang Fuyi backed Yuanqing, while Vice Ministers Gu Dingchen and Huang Wan argued that military action was misguided, and the emperor could not make up his mind. As the siege wore on, the city fell into desperate straits; the rebels tore down the princely residence and government offices for firewood. The Ministry of War issued another pacification order; Yuanqing also raised banners offering surrender, and rebel soldiers began to give themselves up one after another. The ringleaders Huang Zhen and others also came out on successive days, asking that a route be opened for gathering firewood; Yong agreed. The next day, when wood-gatherers came out, Yong had them all arrested. Terror spread through the city; the mutineers rebelled again and called in outside raiders for support. Yong met them in battle, suffered a crushing defeat, and fled. The rebels then ushered more than a dozen mounted raiders into the city, pointed at the Princely Establishment of Dai, and said, "This shall be the nayan's residence." "Nayan" means "great lord" in Chinese. When the townspeople heard this, wailing broke out in every lane. The next day outside raiders assaulted the two southeastern passes while the rebels coordinated in pincer fashion; government troops fought desperately, and both sides suffered killed and wounded. Finding the rebels unreliable, the raiders turned on them, hurled abuse, and withdrew. Meanwhile, raiding cavalry swept south as far as Shuo and Ying. Yuanqing asked to raise troops from the Nine Garrisons and appoint an additional overall commander to hold them off, so that he could devote himself entirely to the siege; the emperor refused. Yuanqing then assaulted the city from every direction, tunneled beneath the walls, and the dead from poisonous smoke lay heaped together. He further proposed damming the water to flood the city. Greatly displeased, the emperor stripped him of office and ordered him to live in retirement, replacing him with Vice Minister of War Zhang Zan. Before Zhang Zan even arrived, Director Zhan Rong and others had already captured all the ringleaders.
38
黃綰勘功罪，言源清、永實罪魁，具劾其婪賄不貲狀。 兵科曾忭等言，宸濠亂，源清有保障功，當蒙八議之貸。 帝怒，下忭等詔獄，逮源清治之。 獄久不決，綰憂去，乃減死，斥為民。 俺答薄京師，即家起之，未赴而卒。 隆慶初，贈兵部尚書。
Huang Wan reviewed the record of merit and blame, declaring Yuanqing and Yong the true instigators, and impeached them in detail for extortionate bribery. Supervising Secretary Zeng Bian and others argued that during Prince Ning's rebellion Yuanqing had distinguished himself in defense and deserved the leniency granted under the Eight Deliberations. Enraged, the emperor sent Bian and the others to the imperial prison and had Yuanqing arrested for trial. The case dragged on without resolution; Wan left office in distress; in the end the death sentence was commuted and Yuanqing was reduced to commoner status. When Altan Khan threatened the capital, Yuanqing was recalled from retirement, but he died before he could report for duty. At the opening of the Longqing reign, he was posthumously honored as Minister of War.
39
劉天和，字養和，麻城人。 正德三年進士。 授南京禮部主事。 劉瑾黜御史十八人，改他曹二十四人補之，天和與焉。 出按陝西。 鎮守中官廖堂奉詔辦食禦物於蘭州，天和謂非所部，辭不往。 堂奏天和拒命，詔逮之。 部民哭送者萬人。 錮詔獄久不釋，吏部尚書楊一清疏救，法司奏當贖杖還職，中旨謫金壇丞。 刑部主事孫繼芳抗章救，不報。 屢遷湖州知府，多惠政。
Liu Tianhe, styled Yanghe, was a native of Macheng. He passed the metropolitan examination in Zhengde 3. He was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites. When Liu Jin dismissed eighteen censors and filled the vacancies with twenty-four men transferred from other offices, Tianhe was among those appointed. He was sent out to inspect Shaanxi. When the eunuch commissioner Liao Tang was ordered by imperial edict to procure imperial provisions at Lanzhou, Tianhe held that the matter lay outside his jurisdiction and refused to go. Tang memorialized that Tianhe had defied orders, and an edict was issued for his arrest. Ten thousand people of the province wept as they escorted him away. Held long in the imperial prison, he was defended in a memorial by Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing; the judicial offices recommended ransom by beating and restoration to office, but a secret edict instead demoted him to assistant magistrate of Jintan. Sun Jifang, a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, submitted an impassioned memorial in his defense, but received no response. After several promotions he became prefect of Huzhou, where he carried out many policies that benefited the people.
40
嘉靖初，擢山西提學副使。 累遷南京太常少卿。 以右僉都御史督甘肅屯政。 請以肅州丁壯及山、陝流民于近邊耕牧，且推行于諸邊。 尋奏當興革者十事，田利大興。 改撫陝西。 請撤鎮守中官及罷為民患者三十余事，帝皆從之。 洮、岷番四十二族蠢動，天和誅不順命者。 又討平湖店大盜及漢中妖賊，就進右副都御史。
At the opening of the Jiajing reign he was promoted to Vice Commissioner for Education in Shanxi. He rose through successive promotions to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to supervise agricultural colonization in Gansu. He proposed settling able-bodied men from Suzhou and displaced people from Shanxi and Shaanxi to farm and herd along the near frontier, and extending the policy to other border regions. He soon submitted a memorial outlining ten reforms to institute or abolish, and agricultural productivity rose sharply. He was transferred to serve as Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi. He petitioned for the removal of eunuch commissioners and the abolition of more than thirty practices that harmed the people; the emperor approved every proposal. When the forty-two Tibetan tribes of Tao and Min grew restless, Tianhe executed those who defied his authority. He also suppressed the major bandits of Pinghu Store and the sorcerer-rebels of Hanzhong, and was promoted on the spot to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
41
母憂，服闋以故官總理河道。 黃河南徙，曆濟、徐皆旁溢。 天和疏汴河，自硃仙鎮至沛飛雲橋，殺其下流。 疏山東七十二泉，自鳧、尼諸山達南旺河，浚其下流。 役夫二萬，不三月訖工。 加工部右侍郎。 故事，河南八府歲役民治河，不赴役者人出銀三兩。 天和因歲饑，請盡蠲旁河受役者課，遠河未役者半之。 詔可。
After observing mourning for his mother, he returned to his former rank to take overall charge of the Grand Canal. The Yellow River shifted eastward, flooding the regions of Ji and Xu on every side. Tianhe dredged the Bian River from Zhuxian Town to Feiyun Bridge in Pei, cutting back its lower channel. He cleared the seventy-two springs of Shandong from Mount Fu, Mount Ni, and neighboring peaks down to the Nanwang River, dredging their lower channels. With twenty thousand laborers, the work was completed in less than three months. He was additionally appointed Right Vice Minister of Works. By precedent the eight prefectures of Henan conscripted the populace each year for river work; those who failed to report for corvée paid three taels of silver apiece. Citing the year's famine, Tianhe asked that levies on those conscripted along the river be fully remitted and that those farther from the river who had not yet served pay only half. The request was approved by edict.
42
十五年改兵部左侍郎，總制三邊軍務。 兵車皆雙輪，用二十人，遇險即困，又行遲不適於用。 天和請仿前總督秦紘只輪車，上置砲槍斧戟，廂前樹狻猊牌，左右虎盾，連二車可蔽三四十人。 一人挽之，推且翼者各二人。 戰則護騎士其中，敵遠則施火器，稍近發弓弩，又近乃出短兵，敵走則騎兵追。 復製隨車小帳，令士不露宿。 又毒弩矢，修邊牆濠塹。 皆從之。
In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of War and given overall command of military affairs on the Three Frontiers. Military wagons all had double wheels and required twenty men to move; they bogged down on difficult terrain and were too slow to be of practical use. Tianhe proposed reviving the single-wheeled cart used by the former overall commander Qin Hong, fitted with cannon, muskets, axes, and halberds, with suanni shields mounted before the carriage box and tiger shields to either side; two carts linked together could shelter thirty or forty men. One man hauled it while two pushed and two flanked it on either side. In battle cavalry sheltered inside; at long range they used firearms, at medium range bows and crossbows, and at close quarters short weapons; when the enemy fled, cavalry gave chase. He also designed small tents to accompany the carts so that soldiers would not have to sleep in the open. He also had crossbow bolts poisoned and had the border wall and moats repaired. All of these proposals were approved.
43
吉囊十萬眾屯賀蘭山後，遣別部寇涼州，副將王輔逐奪其纛。 寇莊浪，總兵官姜奭屢敗之。 進天和右都御史。 寇復大集兵將入犯。 天和策寇瞰西有備必東，密檄延綏副將白爵宵行，與參將吳瑛合。 寇果東入黑河墩，遇爵伏兵，大創而去。 既又入蒺藜川，爵尾擊之，寇多死。 尋入寇家澗、張家塔，為爵、瑛所敗。 犯寧夏者，總兵官王效復破之。 帝大喜，進天和左都御史。 吉囊犯河西，天和禦卻之，進兵部尚書。 寇將入平虜城，天和伏兵花馬池。 寇戰不勝，走河上。 遇伏兵，多死于水。 吉囊乘虛寇固原，剽掠且饜。 會淫潦，弓矢盡膠，無鬥志。 而諸將多畏縮，天和斬指揮二人，召故總兵周尚文令立功。 會陝西總兵官魏時角寇至黑水苑，尚文盡銳夾擊，殺吉囊子小十王。 寇退寧夏，巡撫楊守禮、總兵官任傑等復邀擊，敗之鐵柱泉，斬獲共四百四十餘級。 論功，加天和太子太保，廕一子錦衣千戶，前後齎銀幣十數。 遷南京戶部尚書，召為兵部尚書督團營。 言官論天和衰老，遂乞休歸。 家居三年卒。 贈少保，諡莊襄。
Jinjang encamped with a hundred thousand men behind Helan Mountain and sent a detached force to raid Liangzhou; Vice General Wang Fu pursued them and captured their battle standard. When the raiders entered Zhuanglang, Commander-in-Chief Jiang Shi defeated them repeatedly. Tianhe was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief. The raiders again mustered a large force and prepared to invade. Tianhe reasoned that seeing defenses massed in the west, the raiders would surely strike east; he secretly ordered Yan-sui Vice General Bai Jue to march by night and join Brigade Commander Wu Ying. The raiders did strike east at Heihe Dun, ran into Jue's ambush, suffered heavy losses, and withdrew. They later entered Jili Chuan again; Jue struck from the rear and killed many of them. They soon raided Jiajian and Zhangjiata and were defeated by Jue and Ying. Those who struck at Ningxia were in turn defeated by Commander-in-Chief Wang Xiao. Greatly pleased, the emperor promoted Tianhe to Left Censor-in-Chief. When Jinjang invaded Hexi, Tianhe drove him back and was promoted to Minister of War. As the raiders were about to enter Pinglu City, Tianhe laid an ambush at Huama Chi. Unable to win the battle, the raiders fled toward the river. They ran into the ambush, and many drowned. Jinjang seized the opening to raid Guyuan and looted his fill. Just then torrential rains fell; bows and arrows were rendered useless by the damp, and morale collapsed. Many of the generals hung back in fear; Tianhe executed two commanders and recalled the former commander-in-chief Zhou Shangwen, ordering him to redeem himself in battle. Just as the raiders reached Heishui Garden, Shaanxi Commander-in-Chief Wei Shi and Shangwen threw all their elite forces into a pincer attack and killed Jinjang's son Xiaoshi Wang. As the raiders fell back toward Ningxia, Grand Coordinator Yang Shouli, Commander-in-Chief Ren Jie, and others intercepted them again, defeating them at Tiezhu Spring with more than four hundred and forty heads taken and captives seized. When honors were distributed, Tianhe was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, one son was granted a hereditary post in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and he received silver and silks on more than ten occasions. He was transferred to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing, then recalled to serve as Minister of War and supervise the Tuan battalions. When censorial officials argued that Tianhe had grown too old for office, he requested retirement and returned home. Three years after returning home, he died. He was posthumously made Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Zhuangxiang.
44
天和初舉進士，劉瑾欲與敘宗姓，謝不往。 晚年內召，陶仲文以刺迎，稱戚屬。 天和返其刺曰：「誤矣，吾中外姻連無是人。 」仲文恚，其罷官有力焉。
When Tianhe first passed the metropolitan examination, Liu Jin wanted to claim a kinship with him through their shared surname; Tianhe declined and refused the overture. Late in life he was recalled to the capital; Tao Zhongwen came to meet him with a calling card claiming they were relatives. Tianhe returned the card with the words: "This is a mistake. Among my in-laws inside and outside the court, there is no such person. " Tao Zhongwen was furious and played a significant role in having him removed from office.
45
楊守禮，字秉節，蒲州人。 正德六年進士。 除戶部主事。 嘉靖初，屢遷湖廣僉事。 以計擒公安賊魁。 坐事謫敘州通判。 累遷右副都御史，巡撫四川。 與副將何卿平諸番亂，齎銀幣。 初，守禮貶敘州，為僉事張文奎所辱。 至是，文奎遷四川參議，恐守禮修隙，先以所摭事奏。 詔二人俱解職歸。
Yang Shouli, styled Bingjie, was a native of Puzhou. He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of the Zhengde reign. He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue. At the start of the Jiajing reign he was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang. He devised a stratagem that captured the bandit chieftain of Gong'an. He was demoted to vice prefect of Xuzhou on account of an offense. He rose through repeated promotions to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and Grand Coordinator of Sichuan. Together with Vice General He Qing he pacified the various frontier rebellions and was rewarded with silver and silks. Earlier, when Shouli was demoted to Xuzhou, he was humiliated by Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Wenkui. By then Wenkui had been transferred to Sichuan as a participating secretary. Fearing that Shouli would settle old scores, he preemptively memorialized the throne with accusations he had gathered. An edict ordered both men dismissed from office and sent home.
46
守禮才器敏達，中外以為能。 居家未久，工部尚書秦金等會薦，起河南參政。 再遷右副都御史，巡撫寧夏。 寇犯固原，為總督劉天和所敗。 欲自寧夏去，守禮與總兵任傑等邀敗之。 會天和召還，進守禮右都御史總督軍務代之。 錄前功，進兵部尚書。 總兵官李義、楊信連卻吉囊，三賜璽書銀幣。 尋上疏乞休，帝惡其避難，降俸二級。
Shouli was talented, capable, and quick-witted, and was regarded as able both inside and outside the court. Not long after returning home, Minister of Works Qin Jin and others jointly recommended him, and he was recalled to serve as Administration Vice Commissioner of Henan. He was again promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and appointed Grand Coordinator of Ningxia. When raiders invaded Guyuan, they were defeated by Grand Coordinator Liu Tianhe. As the raiders tried to withdraw from Ningxia, Shouli together with Commander-in-Chief Ren Jie and others intercepted and defeated them. Just then Liu Tianhe was recalled to court, and Shouli was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Right to take over general military affairs in his place. His earlier achievements were recognized, and he was promoted to Minister of War. Commanders-in-Chief Li Yi and Yang Xin repeatedly repulsed Jinjang, and on three occasions the court granted them imperial sealed edicts together with silver and silks. Soon afterward he submitted a memorial requesting retirement. The emperor, angered that he was trying to avoid hardship, reduced his salary by two grades.
47
其秋，寇三萬騎抵綏德。 遊擊張鵬卻之，總兵官吳英等追至塞外，東路參將周文兵亦至，夾擊敗之。 巡按御史殷學言，寇入內地五百里，請治諸將罪。 部議延綏遊兵俱調宣、大，寇方避實擊虛。 而我能以寡勝眾，宜錄其功。 乃加守禮太子少保，學謫外。 守禮尋以憂去。 俺答薄都城，廷臣首以守禮薦，詔趣上道。 寇退，止不行。 久之卒。
That autumn, thirty thousand mounted raiders reached Suide. Mobile Corps Commander Zhang Peng repulsed them; Commander-in-Chief Wu Ying and others pursued them beyond the border; troops under Eastern Route Assistant Regional Commander Zhou Wen also arrived, and in a pincer attack the raiders were defeated. Touring Censor Yin Xue argued that the raiders had penetrated five hundred li into the interior and requested that the generals be punished. The ministry argued that the mobile troops of Yan-Sui had all been transferred to Xuan-Da, and that the raiders had been avoiding strong points to strike weak ones. Yet our forces had defeated a larger enemy with fewer men, and their merit ought to be recognized. Shouli was accordingly made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, while Yin Xue was demoted and sent outside the capital. Shouli soon left office to observe mourning. When Altan approached the capital, court officials were the first to recommend Shouli, and an edict ordered him to set out at once. When the raiders withdrew, the order for him to take up the post was countermanded. After some time he died.
48
張岳，字維喬，惠安人。 自幼好學，以大儒自期。 登正德十一年進士，授行人。 武宗寢疾豹房。 請令大臣侍從，台諫輪直起居，視藥餌，防意外變。 不報。 與同官諫南巡，杖闕下，謫南京國子學正。 世宗嗣位，復故官，遷右司副。 母老乞便養，改南京武選員外郎，曆主客郎中。 方議大禘禮。 張璁求始祖所自出者實之，禮官皆唯唯。 岳言于尚書李時曰：「不如為皇初祖位，毋實以人。 」時大喜，告璁。 璁不謂然，以初議上。 帝竟令題皇初祖主，如嶽言。 璁銜之，出為廣西提學僉事。 行部柳州，軍缺餉大嘩，城閉五日。 嶽令守城啟門，召詰嘩者予餉去。 尋以計擒首惡，置之理。 入賀，改提學江西。 不謝璁，璁黜廣西選貢七人，謫嶽廣東鹽課提舉。 遷廉州知府。 督民墾棄地，教以桔槔運水。 廉民多盜珠池。 岳居四年，未嘗入一珠。
Zhang Yue, styled Weiqiao, was a native of Huian. From childhood he loved learning and aspired to become a great Confucian scholar. He passed the metropolitan examination in the eleventh year of the Zhengde reign and was appointed an attendant. Emperor Wuzong lay gravely ill in the Leopard Quarter. He requested that senior ministers attend the emperor, that censorial and remonstrance officials take turns watching over his daily care and medicines, and that precautions be taken against any unforeseen turn of events. No response was given. Together with his colleagues he remonstrated against the southern tour; he was beaten at the palace gate and demoted to director of study at the Nanjing Imperial Academy. When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, Yue was restored to his former post and promoted to Right Division Vice Director. His mother was elderly, and he requested a post that would allow him to care for her conveniently; he was transferred to Assistant Department Director of the Military Selection Bureau at Nanjing and later served as bureau director of Receptions. At that time the court was debating the grand di ritual. Zhang Cong sought to identify and substantiate the progenitor from whom the dynastic founder descended, and the ritual officials all assented without objection. Yue said to Minister Li Shi: "It would be better to establish a place for the Founding Progenitor of the Emperor, without assigning a specific person to it. " Li Shi was greatly pleased and told Zhang Cong. Cong disagreed and submitted the original proposal to the throne. The emperor ultimately ordered the spirit tablet inscribed as the Founding Progenitor of the Emperor, just as Yue had proposed. Cong bore a grudge against him and had him sent out to serve as Education Intendant of Guangxi. While on an inspection tour in Liuzhou, troops who had not received their pay raised a great uproar, and the city gates remained closed for five days. Yue ordered the gate guards to open the city, summoned the rioters for questioning, paid them their arrears, and sent them away. Soon afterward he devised a stratagem that captured the ringleaders and brought them to justice. When he entered the capital to offer congratulations, he was transferred to education intendant of Jiangxi. Yue did not thank Zhang Cong, so Cong dismissed seven selected tribute students from Guangxi and demoted Yue to Salt Tax Commissioner of Guangdong. He was transferred to serve as prefect of Lianzhou. He supervised the people in reclaiming abandoned land and taught them to use the shaduf to lift water for irrigation. The people of Lianzhou frequently poached from the pearl fisheries. In four years as prefect, Yue never accepted a single pearl.
49
帝使使往安南詰莫登庸殺主，岳言于總督張經曰：「莫氏篡黎，可無勘而知也，使往受謾詞辱國，請留使者毋前。 」經不可。 知欽州林希元上書請決討莫氏，嶽貽書止之，復條上不可討六事。 為書貽執政曰：「據邊民報，黎賙襲封無嗣，以兄子譓為子。 陳暠作亂，賙遇害，暠篡。 未幾國人擁立譓，暠奔諒山。 訁惠立七年，為莫登庸所逼，出居昇華。 登庸立譓幼弟騑而相之，卒弑騑自立，國分為三。 黎在南，莫居中，陳在西北。 後諒山亦為登庸有，陳遂絕。 而黎所居即古日南地，與占城鄰，限大海，登庸不能逾之南，故兩存。 近登庸又以交州付其孫福海，而自營海東府地都齋居之。 蓋安南諸府，惟海東地最大，即所謂王山郡也。 此賊負篡逆名，常練兵備我，又時揚言求入貢。 邊人以非故王也，弗敢聞。 愚以為彼內亂未嘗有所侵犯，可且置之，待其亂定乃貢。 若必用兵，勝負利純非嶽所敢知。 」執政得書不能決。 已，毛伯溫來視師，張經一以軍事委嶽。 又以翁萬達才，進二人于伯溫。 岳與伯溫語數日，伯溫曰：「交事屬君矣。 」許登庸如嶽議。 會嶽遷浙江提學副使，又遷參政，伯溫馳奏留之，乃改廣東參政，分守海北。 登庸降，加嶽俸一級，賜銀幣。 尋以征瓊州叛黎功，加俸及賜如之。
The emperor dispatched an envoy to Annam to inquire into Mo Dangyong's murder of the ruler. Yue said to Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing: "The Mo clan usurped the Li dynasty—one need not investigate to know that. If the envoy goes, he will only accept evasive words and humiliate the state. Please detain the envoy and do not let him proceed. " Zhang Jing would not agree. Lin Xiyuan, prefect of Qinzhou, submitted a memorial requesting a decisive campaign against the Mo clan. Yue wrote to dissuade him and also listed six reasons why such a campaign should not be undertaken. He wrote to the chief ministers: "According to reports from border people, Li Ku inherited the title but had no heir and adopted his elder brother's son Hui as his own. Chen Gao raised a rebellion; Li Ku was killed, and Gao usurped the throne. Before long the people installed Hui as ruler, and Gao fled to Lang Son. Hui had reigned seven years when Mo Dangyong forced him out; he withdrew to reside at Sheng Hua. Dangyong installed Hui's younger brother Fei and acted as regent, but in the end he assassinated Fei and seized the throne himself, and the country split into three parts. The Li held the south, the Mo the center, and the Chen the northwest. Later Lang Son also fell to Dangyong, and the Chen line came to an end. The Li domain occupied the ancient Rinan territory, bordering Champa and bounded by the sea; Dangyong could not cross south of it, and so both regimes survived. Recently Dangyong also handed Jiaozhou over to his grandson Fuhai, while he himself took up residence at Didu in Hai Dong prefecture. Of all the prefectures in Annam, Hai Dong had the largest territory—the so-called Wangshan commandery. This rebel bears the stigma of usurpation and treason; he constantly drills troops against us and from time to time announces that he wishes to offer tribute. Border officials, knowing he was not the former king, dared not report it to the court. I believe that although they are torn by internal disorder, they have not invaded us; we may set the matter aside for now and wait until their turmoil subsides before accepting tribute. If force must be used, the outcome and whether it would bring gain or loss are not matters I dare presume to judge. " The chief ministers received the letter but could not reach a decision. Before long Mao Bowen arrived to inspect the army, and Zhang Jing wholly entrusted military affairs to Yue. He also recommended Weng Wanda for his talent and presented both men to Mao Bowen. Yue spoke with Mao Bowen for several days, and Bowen said: "The Annam affair is yours to manage. " It was agreed that Dangyong would comply with Yue's proposal. Just as Yue was transferred to Vice Education Intendant of Zhejiang and then to Administration Vice Commissioner, Mao Bowen urgently memorialized to retain him; he was then reassigned as Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, with charge of the Haibei circuit. When Dangyong surrendered, Yue's salary was raised one grade and he was granted silver and silks. Soon afterward, for his merit in suppressing the rebel Li of Qiongzhou, he received the same salary increase and rewards.
50
塞上多事，言官薦岳邊才。 伯溫言：「岳可南，翁萬達可北也。 」遂擢嶽右僉都御史，撫治鄖陽。 旋移撫江西，進右副都御史，總督兩廣軍務兼巡撫。 討破廣東封川僮蘇公樂等，進兵部右侍郎。 平廣西馬平諸縣瑤賊，先後俘斬四千，招撫二萬餘人，誅賊魁韋金田等，增俸一級。 召為刑部右侍郎，以御史徐南金言命留任。 連山賊李金與賀縣賊倪仲亮等，出沒衡、永、郴、桂，積三十年不能平，嶽大合兵討擒之。 蒞鎮四年，巨寇悉平，召拜兵部左侍郎。
With trouble mounting on the frontier, censorial officials recommended Yue for his frontier expertise. Mao Bowen said: "Yue can serve in the south, and Weng Wanda in the north. " Yue was accordingly promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and appointed Pacification Commissioner of Yunyang. He was soon transferred to serve as grand coordinator of Jiangxi, promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right, and given overall military affairs in the two Guang with concurrent duties as grand coordinator. He campaigned against and defeated the Yao bandits Su Gongle and others of Fengchuan in Guangdong, and was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of War. He pacified the Yao bandits of Maping and other counties in Guangxi; in all four thousand were captured or beheaded, more than twenty thousand were brought in through appeasement, bandit chiefs including Wei Jintian were executed, and his salary was raised one grade. He was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Justice, but on the recommendation of Censor Xu Nanjin the order was changed and he was kept in his post. Li Jin, bandit leader of Lianshan, and Ni Zhongliang of Hexian and others had raided across Heng, Yong, Chen, and Gui for thirty years without being suppressed; Yue massed troops, campaigned against them, and captured them. After four years in his post all major bandits had been suppressed, and he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Left in the Ministry of War.
51
湖貴間有山曰蠟爾，諸苗居之。 東屬鎮溪千戶所筸子坪長官司，隸湖廣； 西屬銅仁、平頭二長官司，隸貴州； 北接四川酉陽，廣袤數百里。 諸苗數反，官兵不能制。 侍郎萬鏜征之，四年不克。 乃授其魁龍許保冠帶。 湖苗暫息，而貴苗反如故。 鏜班師，龍許保及其党吳黑苗復亂。 貴州巡撫李義壯告警，乃命岳總督湖廣、貴州、四川軍務，討之。 進右都御史。 義壯持鏜議欲撫，嶽劾其阻兵，罷之。 先義壯撫貴州者，僉都御史王學益與鏜附嚴嵩，主撫議，數從中撓嶽。 嶽持益堅。 許保襲執印江知縣徐文伯及石阡推官鄧本忠以去，嶽坐停俸。 乃使總兵官沈希儀、參將石邦憲等分道進，躬入銅仁督之。 先後斬賊魁五十三人，獨許保、黑苗跳不獲。 岳以捷聞，言貴苗漸平，湖苗聽撫，請遣土兵歸農，朝議許之。 未幾，酉陽宣慰冉元嗾許保、黑苗突思州，劫執知府李允簡。 邦憲兵邀奪允簡還，允簡竟死。 嵩父子故憾岳，欲逮治之，徐階持不可。 乃奪右都御史，以兵部侍郎督師。 邦憲等旋破賊。 岳搜山箐，餘賊獻思州印及許保。 湖廣兵亦破擒首惡李通海等。 岳以黑苗未獲，不敢報功。 已而冉元謀露，嶽發其奸。 元賄嚴世蕃責岳絕苗黨。 邦憲竟得黑苗以獻，苗患乃息。
Between Huguang and Guizhou there is a mountain called La'er, where various Miao peoples dwell. To the east it fell under the Gaoziping native office of Zhenxi Guard, subordinate to Huguang; to the west it fell under the two native offices of Tongren and Pingtou, subordinate to Guizhou; to the north it adjoined Youyang in Sichuan, and stretched several hundred li across. The Miao there rebelled repeatedly, and government troops could not suppress them. Vice Minister Wan Ying campaigned against them for four years without success. The chieftain Long Xubao was then granted an official cap and belt as a mark of recognition. The Miao in Huguang temporarily quieted down, but those in Guizhou rose in rebellion again as before. When Wan Ying withdrew his army, Long Xubao and his follower Wu Heimiao rebelled once more. Grand Coordinator of Guizhou Li Yizhuang reported the emergency, and Zhang Yue was ordered to take overall military affairs in Huguang, Guizhou, and Sichuan and campaign against the rebels. He was promoted to the post of Censor-in-Chief of the Right. Li Yizhuang upheld Wan Ying's proposal to appease the rebels, but Zhang Yue impeached him for obstructing military action and had him removed from office. Wang Xueyi, Vice Censor-in-Chief, who had preceded Li Yizhuang in pacifying Guizhou, together with Wan Ying had attached himself to Yan Song, advocated appeasement, and repeatedly interfered with Zhang Yue from within the court. Zhang Yue held all the more firmly to his position. Xubao raided and seized Magistrate of Yinjiang Xu Wenbo and Push Official of Shiqian Deng Benzhong and carried them off, and Zhang Yue was punished with suspension of salary. He then sent Commander-in-Chief Shen Xiyi, Assistant Regional Commander Shi Bangxian, and others to advance by separate routes, while he personally entered Tongren to direct operations. In succession fifty-three bandit chiefs were beheaded, but Xubao and Heimiao alone escaped and could not be captured.
