Zhang Yue reported the victory, stating that the Guizhou Miao were gradually being pacified and the Huguang Miao were willing to submit to appeasement; he requested that native troops be sent back to their farms, and the court approved. Before long, Pacification Commissioner of Youyang Ran Yuan incited Xubao and Heimiao to raid Sizhou and abduct Prefect Li Yunjian. Shi Bangxian's troops intercepted the raiders and recovered Li Yunjian, but Yunjian died in the end. Yan Song and his son bore an old grudge against Zhang Yue and wished to have him arrested and punished, but Xu Jie argued against it. Zhang Yue was accordingly stripped of the title Censor-in-Chief of the Right and retained as Vice Minister of War to direct the army. Shi Bangxian and the others soon defeated the bandits. Zhang Yue searched the mountain ravines, and the remaining bandits surrendered the seal of Sizhou and turned over Xubao. Huguang troops also defeated the rebels and captured the ringleaders Li Tonghai and others. Because Heimiao had not yet been captured, Zhang Yue did not dare report his achievements. Before long Ran Yuan's plot was exposed, and Zhang Yue revealed his treachery. Ran Yuan bribed Yan Shifan to rebuke Zhang Yue for cutting off ties with the Miao faction. Shi Bangxian in the end captured Heimiao and presented him to the court, and the Miao trouble then ceased.

岳卒於沅州。 喪歸，沅人迎哭者不絕。 已，敘功，復右都御史，贈太子少保，諡襄惠。
Zhang Yue died at Yuanzhou. When his coffin returned home, the people of Yuan came out to weep along the route without cease. Later his achievements were recognized; he was posthumously restored as Censor-in-Chief of the Right, granted the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and given the posthumous title Xianghui.
53
岳博覽，工文章，經術湛深，不喜王守仁學，以程、硃為宗。
Zhang Yue was broadly learned, skilled in literary composition, and deeply versed in classical learning; he did not favor the teachings of Wang Shouren and took the Cheng-Zhu school as his standard.

李允簡，融縣人。 由舉人起家。 以郡境多寇，道孥歸，獨與孫炳文居。 祖孫皆被執，許保挾以求厚贖。 允簡則傳語邦憲令亟進兵。 在賊中自投高崖下，賊拽出，棄之途。 思人舁還，至清浪衛而卒。 詔贈貴州副使，賜祭葬，官一子。
Li Yunjian was a native of Rong County. He rose through the provincial examination. Because the prefecture was troubled by many bandits, he sent his wife and children home along the way and lived alone with his grandson Bingwen. Both grandfather and grandson were seized, and Xubao held them hostage to demand a heavy ransom. Li Yunjian, for his part, sent word to Shi Bangxian ordering him to advance troops at once. While held by the bandits he threw himself from a high cliff; they pulled him out and left him on the road. The people of Sizhou carried him back, but he died upon reaching Qinglang Guard. An edict posthumously granted him the rank of Vice Commissioner of Guizhou, bestowed sacrificial rites and burial honors, and appointed one of his sons to office.

郭宗皋，字君弼，福山人。 嘉靖八年進士。 選庶起士。 尋詔與選者皆改除，得刑部主事。 擢御史。 十二年十月，星隕如雨。 未幾，哀沖太子薨，大同兵亂。 宗皋勸帝惇崇寬厚，察納忠言，勿專以嚴明為治。 帝大怒，下詔獄，杖四十釋之。 曆按蘇、松、順天。 行部乘馬，不禦肩輿。 會廷推保定巡撫劉夔還理院事，宗皋論夔嘗薦大學士李時子，諂媚無行，不任風紀，坐奪俸兩月。 尋出為雁門兵備副使，轉陝西參政，遷大理少卿。
Guo Zonggao, styled Junbi, was a native of Fushan. He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighth year of the Jiajing reign. He was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor. Soon an edict ordered all those selected to be reassigned, and he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice. He was elevated to censor. In the tenth month of the twelfth year, stars fell like rain across the sky. Before long Crown Prince Aichong died, and the garrison at Datong mutinied. Guo Zonggao urged the emperor to esteem and practice generosity and magnanimity, discern and accept loyal counsel, and not govern solely through severity and rigor. The emperor was greatly angered, had him sent to the imperial prison, beaten forty strokes, and then released. He served in turn as touring censor of Suzhou, Songjiang, and Shuntian. When touring his jurisdiction he rode horseback and refused a sedan chair. When the court recommended Grand Coordinator of Baoding Liu Kui to return and handle affairs at the censorate, Guo Zonggao argued that Liu Kui had once recommended the son of Grand Secretary Li Shi, was fawning and without integrity, and was unfit for censorial discipline; Zonggao was punished with two months' salary withheld. He was soon sent out as Military Defense Vice Commissioner of Yanmen, transferred to Administration Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi, and promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

二十三年十月，寇入萬全右衛，抵廣昌，列營四十里。 順天巡撫硃方下獄，擢宗皋右僉都御史代之，寇已去。 宗皋言：「密雲最要害，宜宿重兵。 乞敕馬蘭、太平、燕河三屯歲發千人，以五月赴密雲，有警則總兵官自將赴援。 居庸、白楊，地要兵弱，遇警必待部奏，不能及事。 請預擬借調之法，令建昌三屯軍，平時則協助密雲，遇警則移駐居庸。 」俱報可。 久之，宗皋聞敵騎四十萬欲分道入，奏調京營、山東、河南兵為援。 已竟無實，坐奪俸一年。 故事，京營歲發五軍詣薊鎮防秋。 宗皋請罷三軍，以其犒軍銀充本鎮募兵費。 又請發修邊餘銀，增築燕河營、古北口。 帝疑有侵冒，令罷歸聽勘。 既而事得白。 起故官，巡撫大同，與宣府巡撫李仁易鎮。
In the tenth month of the twenty-third year, raiders entered Wanquan Right Guard, reached Guangchang, and pitched camps in a line forty li long. Grand Coordinator of Shuntian Zhu Fang was imprisoned; Guo Zonggao was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right to replace him, but the raiders had already withdrawn. Guo Zonggao said: "Miyun is the most critical point and ought to hold a strong garrison. I beg that orders be issued for the three garrisons of Malan, Taiping, and Yanhe to dispatch one thousand men each year in the fifth month to Miyun; when alarm arises the commander-in-chief shall personally lead reinforcements. Juyong and Baiyang are strategically vital yet weakly garrisoned; in an emergency one must wait for a ministry memorial and cannot act in time. I request that a method of advance transfer be established, so that the three garrisons of Jianchang assist Miyun in peacetime and shift to garrison Juyong in an emergency. All were approved. After some time Guo Zonggao heard that four hundred thousand enemy horsemen intended to enter by separate routes and memorialized to transfer troops from the capital garrison, Shandong, and Henan as reinforcements. In the end there proved to be no truth to it, and he was punished with one year's salary withheld. By established practice the capital garrison dispatched five armies to Jizhen each year for autumn defense. Guo Zonggao requested that three armies be abolished and their troop-reward silver used to fund recruitment in the local command. He also requested that surplus silver from border repairs be used to expand Yanhe Camp and Gubeikou. The emperor suspected embezzlement and ordered him to leave office and return home pending investigation. Before long he was cleared of wrongdoing. He was recalled to his former rank, appointed grand coordinator of Datong, and exchanged posts with Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu Li Ren.

尋進兵部右侍郎，總督宣、大、山西軍務。 俺答三萬騎犯萬全左衛，總兵官陳鳳、副總兵林椿與戰鷂兒嶺，殺傷相當，宗皋坐奪俸。 明年再犯大同，總兵官張達及椿皆戰死，宗皋與巡撫陳燿坐奪俸。 給事中唐禹追論死事狀，因言全軍悉陷，乃數十年未有之大衄。 帝乃逮宗皋及燿，各杖一百，燿遂死，宗皋戍陝西靖虜衛。
Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of War and given overall military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi. Altan with thirty thousand mounted raiders invaded Wanquan Left Guard; Commanders-in-Chief Chen Feng and Vice Commander Lin Chun fought them at Yao'er Ridge with roughly equal casualties, and Guo Zonggao was punished with salary withheld. The next year they invaded Datong again; Commanders-in-Chief Zhang Da and Lin Chun both died in battle, and Guo Zonggao and Grand Coordinator Chen Yao were punished with salary withheld. Supervising Secretary Tang Yu reviewed the circumstances of the deaths and argued that the entire army had been lost—the greatest defeat in decades. The emperor then arrested Guo Zonggao and Chen Yao; each was beaten one hundred strokes; Chen Yao then died, and Guo Zonggao was exiled to serve at Jinglu Guard in Shaanxi.

隆慶改元，從戍所起刑部右侍郎，改兵部，協理戎政。 旋進南京右都御史，就改兵部尚書參贊機務。 給事中莊國禎劾宗皋衰庸，宗皋亦自以年老求去，詔許之。 萬曆中，再存問，歲給廩隸。 十六年，宗皋年九十，又遣行人存問。 是年卒。 贈太子太保，諡康介。
At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was recalled from exile as Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Justice, transferred to the Ministry of War, and put in charge of military administration. Soon he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Right at Nanjing and then reassigned as Minister of War with concurrent duties assisting in state affairs. Supervising Secretary Zhuang Guozhen impeached Guo Zonggao as decrepit and incompetent; Guo Zonggao also, considering himself old, requested retirement, and an edict granted it. During the Wanli reign he was twice sent imperial greetings and granted an annual stipend and attendants. In the sixteenth year Guo Zonggao was ninety, and an attendant was again dispatched to inquire after him. He died that year. He was posthumously made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Kangjie.

趙時春，字景仁，平涼人。 幼與群兒嬉，輒列旗幟，部勒如兵法。 年十四舉於鄉。 逾四年，為嘉靖五年，會試第一。 選庶起士。 以張璁言改官，得戶部主事。 尋轉兵部。 九年七月，上疏曰：「陛下以災變求言已旬月，大小臣工率浮詞面謾。 蓋自靈寶知縣言河清受賞，都御史汪鋐繼進甘露，今副都御史徐贊、訓導范仲斌進瑞麥，指揮張楫進嘉禾，鋐及御史楊東又進鹽華，禮部尚書李時再請表賀。 仲斌等不足道，鋐、贊司風紀，時典三禮，乃罔上欺君，壞風傷政。 」帝責其妄言，且令獻讜言善策。 時春惶恐引咎未對。 帝趣之，於是時春上言：
Zhao Shichun, styled Jingren, was a native of Pingliang. Even as a child at play with other boys, he would set out banners and flags and drill them as if by military rule. At the age of fourteen he passed the provincial examination. Four years later, in the fifth year of the Jiajing reign, he ranked first in the metropolitan examination. He was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor. On Zhang Cong's recommendation his appointment was changed, and he became a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue. He was soon transferred to the Ministry of War. In the seventh month of the ninth year he submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has sought counsel on account of calamities and portents for a full month, yet officials great and small mostly offer empty words and deceit to your face. Since the magistrate of Lingbao spoke of the river clearing and received a reward, Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong successively presented sweet dew; now Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Zan and Instructor Fan Zhongbin have presented auspicious wheat, Commander Zhang Ji has presented fine grain, Wang Hong and Censor Yang Dong have again presented salt flowers, and Minister of Rites Li Shi has again requested a congratulatory memorial. Fan Zhongbin and the like are not worth mentioning, but Wang Hong and Xu Zan oversee censorial discipline and Li Shi presides over the three ritual codes—yet they deceive the ruler above and harm customs and government. The emperor rebuked him for reckless speech and ordered him to submit loyal counsel and sound policies. Zhao Shichun, in fear and self-reproach, had not yet replied. The emperor pressed him, and thereupon Zhao Shichun submitted his words:
60
當今之務最大者有四，最急者有三。 最大者，曰崇治本。 君之喜怒，賞罰所自出，勿以逆心事為可怒，則賞罰大公而天下治。 曰信號令。 無信一人之言，必參諸公論； 毋狃一時之近，必稽之永遠。 苟利十而害一，則利不必興； 功百而費半，則功不必舉。 如是而天下享安靜之福矣。 曰廣延訪。 宜仿古人輪對及我朝宣召之制，使大臣、台諫、侍從各得敷納殿陛間，群吏則以其職事召問之。 曰勵廉恥。 大臣宜待以禮，取大節略小過。 台諫言是者用之，非者寬容之。 庶臣工自愛，不敢不勵。
Among the tasks of the present day, the greatest number four, and the most urgent three. Of the greatest matters: first, honor the root of governance. The ruler's joy and anger are the source from which rewards and punishments proceed; do not treat unwelcome matters as grounds for anger, and rewards and punishments will be broadly fair and the realm will be well governed. Second, have faith in commands and edicts. Do not trust the word of a single person; it must be weighed against public opinion; do not cling to what is immediately at hand; it must be examined in light of the long term. If benefit is ten and harm one, the benefit need not be pursued; if achievement is a hundred and cost half, the achievement need not be undertaken. Then the realm will enjoy the blessing of peace and quiet. Third, extend consultation broadly. One ought to follow the ancient system of rotating audience and our dynasty's system of imperial summons, so that senior ministers, censorial and remonstrance officials, and attendants may each expound and offer counsel in the imperial hall, while the various officials are summoned and questioned according to their duties. Fourth, encourage integrity and a sense of shame. Great ministers should be treated with ritual propriety, honoring their essential integrity while overlooking minor faults. When censors and remonstrators speak what is right, employ their counsel; when they do not, be tolerant. In this way officials will value their standing and not dare fail to exert themselves.
61
其最急者，曰惜人才。 凡得罪諸臣，其才不當棄，其過或可原，宜霈然發命，召還故秩。 且因南郊禮成，除謫戍之罪，與之更始。 曰固邊圉。 敗軍之律宜嚴，臨陣而退者，裨將得以戮士卒，大將得以戮裨將，總制官得以戮大將，則人心震悚，而所向用命。 曰正治教。 請復古冠婚、喪祭之禮，絕醮祭、禱祀之術。 凡佛老之徒有假引符籙、依託經懺、幻化黃白、飛升遐景以冒寵祿者，即賜遣斥，則正道修明而民志定。
Among the most urgent matters is this: cherish human talent. For all ministers who have offended, their talent should not be discarded and their faults may be forgiven; a broad edict should summon them back to their former ranks. Moreover, when the southern suburban rites are completed, remit the crimes of those banished to frontier garrison duty and give them a fresh start. Next: secure the frontier. The laws governing defeated armies should be strict: when men retreat in battle, assistant generals may execute soldiers, generals may execute assistant generals, and supreme commanders may execute generals—then hearts will be awed and troops will obey in action. Next: rectify governance and instruction. Please restore the ancient rites of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice, and abolish Daoist offerings and prayer rituals. All followers of Buddhism and Daoism who falsely cite talismans, rely on scripture recitation, conjure gold and silver, or claim ascension to distant realms in order to usurp favor and salary should at once be dismissed and expelled; then the orthodox Way will be cultivated and the people's will settled.

帝覽之，益怒，下詔獄掠治，黜為民。 久之，選東宮官屬，起翰林編修兼司經局校書。
The emperor read it, grew still angrier, had him thrown into the imperial prison and tortured under interrogation, and reduced him to commoner status. After a long while, when selecting Eastern Palace staff, he was raised as Hanlin compiler and concurrently proofreader in the Classics Bureau.

帝有疾，時春與羅洪先、唐順之疏請東宮禦殿，受百官正旦朝賀。 帝大怒，復黜為民。 京師被寇，朝議以時春知兵，起兵部主事，贊理京營務，統民兵訓練。 大將軍仇鸞倡馬市，時春憤曰：「此秦檜續耳。 身為大將，而效市儈，可乎？ 」忤鸞，為所構，幾重得罪。 稍遷山東僉事，進副使。
When the emperor fell ill, Shichun together with Luo Hongxian and Tang Shunzhi memorialized requesting that the heir apparent preside in the hall and receive the New Year's court congratulations of all officials. The emperor was greatly enraged and again reduced him to commoner status. When the capital was raided, the court held that Shichun understood military affairs; he was raised to principal clerk in the Ministry of War, assisted in managing capital garrison affairs, and commanded militia training. Grand general Qiu Luan advocated the horse markets; Shichun said in anger, "This is but a continuation of Qin Hui. To be a great general and yet act like a market peddler—can that be right? " He offended Luan, was framed by him, and nearly suffered heavy punishment. He was gradually transferred to surveillance commissioner of Shandong and advanced to vice commissioner.

三十二年，擢僉都御史，巡撫山西。 時春慷慨負奇氣，善騎射。 慨寇縱橫，將帥不任職，數謂人：「使吾領選卒五千，俺答、邱福不足平也。 」作《禦寇論》，論戰守甚悉。 既秉節鉞，益思以武功自奮。 其年九月，寇入神池、利民諸堡，時春率馬步兵往禦之。 至廣武，諸將畢會。 謀報寇騎二千餘，去兩舍。 時春擐甲欲馳，大將李淶固止之。 時春大言曰：「賊知吾來必遁，緩追即不及。 」遂策馬前。 及於大蟲嶺，伏兵四起，敗績。 倉皇投一墩，守卒縋之上乃得免，淶軍竟覆。 被論，解官聽調。 時春喜談兵，至是一戰而敗。 然當是時將帥率避寇不擊。 為督撫者安居堅城，遙領軍事，無躬搏寇者。 時春功雖不就，天下皆壯其氣。
In the thirty-second year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Shanxi. Shichun was generous and possessed an extraordinary spirit; he was skilled in horsemanship and archery. Lamenting that raiders ranged freely and generals failed in their duties, he often told people, "If I were given command of five thousand picked troops, Altan and Qiu Fu would be nothing to pacify. " He wrote the Treatise on Repelling Bandits, discussing offense and defense in great detail. Once he held the commander's tally, he thought all the more to distinguish himself by military achievement. That year in the ninth month, raiders entered the forts of Shenchi, Limin, and others; Shichun led cavalry and infantry to repel them. At Guangwu all the generals assembled. Scouts reported more than two thousand enemy horsemen, two stages away. Shichun donned armor and wished to charge; general Li Qing firmly stopped him. Shichun spoke loudly, "When the bandits know I have come they will surely flee; if we delay pursuit we will not catch them. " He then spurred his horse forward. At Dachong Ridge ambush troops rose on every side and he suffered defeat. In panic he fled to a beacon tower; the garrison soldiers hauled him up by rope before he escaped, while Qing's army was utterly destroyed. He was impeached, stripped of office, and held awaiting reassignment. Shichun loved to discuss military affairs; now one battle brought defeat. Yet at that time generals generally avoided the raiders and would not attack. Those serving as supreme commanders and grand coordinators dwelt secure in strong cities, directed military affairs from afar, and none personally grappled with the enemy. Though Shichun's achievement did not succeed, all under Heaven admired his spirit.
65
時春讀書善強記，文章豪肆，與唐順之、王慎中齊名。 詩，伉浪自喜類其為人。
Shichun had a strong memory in reading; his essays were bold and expansive, and he was famed alongside Tang Shunzhi and Wang Shenzhong. In poetry he was proud and unrestrained, pleased with himself in a manner that matched his character.
66
贊曰：姚鏌等封疆宣其擘畫，軍務暢其機謀，勳績咸有可紀。 伍文定從王守仁平宸濠之難，厥功最懋。 趙時春將略自命，一出輒躓。 夫危事而易言之，固知兵者所弗取乎。
The eulogy says: Yao Mo and the others in frontier administration proclaimed their planning, in military affairs their stratagems flowed freely, and their achievements are all worth recording. Wu Wending followed Wang Shouren in pacifying the crisis of Chen Hao; his merit was the greatest. Zhao Shichun styled himself a strategist; once he went forth he stumbled. To speak lightly of perilous affairs—surely those who understand warfare will not approve of that.
